pool.md:
# Keen Edge

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Id | `keen-edge` |
| Rarity | Common (bone ink `#cfc8b6`), 4 levels |
| Kind | Mods (a plain number) |
| Trigger | None: always on (no `when`; raises the `damage` mod) |
| Origin | Kept from js/data/abilities.js: same numbers and text; gains `plain: true` and the edge glint. |

## Card

**{damage} more damage.** (3 words, 14 chars; level I reads "8% more damage.")

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): keep the current `ABILITY_ICONS['keen-edge']`, a sword on the diagonal with a small plus beside it.
- Hover loop (1.4 s): one stroke: a blade sweeps across the card (0.3 s), a thin white line races along its edge (0.2 s); hold, fade.

## Idea

The plain damage pick, kept because a run needs one honest number. Every other common asks you to do something; this one only asks you to keep swinging. Its touch is that you can see it: the blade's edge catches a hair-thin white glint on every swing, and at level IV a faint bone-ink streak trails it, so a friend watching can tell your blade is the sharper one.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'keen-edge', name: 'Keen Edge', rarity: 'common', plain: true,
  text: '{damage} more damage.', mods: true,
  levels: [{ damage: 0.08 }, { damage: 0.16 }, { damage: 0.24 }, { damage: 0.32 }] },
```

Numbers: a fight is about 40-60 landed blows (light 16, full heavy about 61, counter about 40), so 1600-3200 damage solo. Level I adds about 130-250 a fight; level IV about 500-1000. This is the yardstick every other common is measured against: about 100-250 damage a fight, or the same worth in safety, at level I.

## Engine work

- None for the number: `damage` is an existing `ABILITY_MODS` key, applied in `abilityStrike`.
- New field `plain: true` (shared by the eight plain commons): the offer draws a plain common at `CONFIG.abilities.plainWeight` (0.5) of a common's weight, so plain numbers come up less often (PLAN item 6). `validate.js`: `plain` is only `true`, and only on a `mods` common.
- The glint: drawing only, on the existing `attackPhase` event (`phase: 'active'`) for the local player's attacks, its brightness read from `kit.mods.damage`.

## Multiplayer

Unchanged: the server already sums the holder's `damage` mod into their blows. The glint is drawn by every browser on that player's blade (it reads their kit, which each browser has). It touches no teammate.

## Effect

Layered, timed from each attack's active frame (t = 0):

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00 | Glint | A hair-thin white line runs along the blade edge from hilt to tip, on the existing blade-trail mesh (a brighter edge row in its texture, no new mesh) | `#f4f1e8` core, `#cfc8b6` edge |
| 0.00-0.18 | Run | The line's bright point slides hilt to tip; brightness 0.4 / 0.55 / 0.7 / 0.85 by level | as above |
| 0.05-0.35 (level IV only) | Streak | A faint bone-ink after-streak, one flat stroke behind the swing's arc, tapering, dark ink outline | `#cfc8b6` body, `#16130f` outline |

Budget (Common class): 1 pooled mesh (the streak; the glint lives on the existing trail), 0 particles, no light, no ribbon, no impact frame. Peak 0.18 s. Reduced motion: no change needed (no flash; the line is steady, not flickering).

## Sound

None. It plays on every swing, where a sound would be noise; the swing's own sound carries it.

## Camera

No camera kick: commons never take one.

## Images

- `img/keen-edge-1.webp`: the swordsman mid-swing, a razor-thin white glint racing along the edge of the blade, a faint bone-coloured ink streak trailing it.

pool.md:
# Iron Blood

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Id | `iron-blood` |
| Rarity | Common (bone ink `#cfc8b6`), 4 levels |
| Kind | Mods (a plain number) |
| Trigger | None: always on (no `when`; raises the `maxHp` mod) |
| Origin | Kept from js/data/abilities.js: trimmed from 10/20/30/40% to 8/16/24/32%; gains `plain: true`, the iron rim and the clank. |

## Card

**{maxHp} more health.** (3 words, 14 chars; level I reads "8% more health.")

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): keep the current `ABILITY_ICONS['iron-blood']`, a heart with a plus inside.
- Hover loop (1.4 s): one stroke: a short bar fills left to right (0.4 s), a second, darker line closes round it as a rim (0.3 s); hold, fade.

## Idea

More health, the safest pick for a friend still learning the bosses. It was trimmed a little because health picks carried runs further than damage picks did (PLAN item 11). Its touch marks the moment you take it: dark iron veins show under the skin of the forearm for a breath with a heavy clank, and from then on your health bar wears a dark iron rim, so you and your friends can see who is the sturdy one.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'iron-blood', name: 'Iron Blood', rarity: 'common', plain: true,
  text: '{maxHp} more health.', mods: true,
  levels: [{ maxHp: 0.08 }, { maxHp: 0.16 }, { maxHp: 0.24 }, { maxHp: 0.32 }] },
```

Numbers: the bar is 120, so level I is about 10 more health and level IV about 38. A boss blow is mostly 20-40, so level I is a third of a blow and level IV about one more blow survived a life. Flask heals stay flat (45), so the larger bar also means each flask covers less of it: the trim keeps it from out-carrying Keen Edge.

## Engine work

- None for the number: `maxHp` is an existing `ABILITY_MODS` key (the server's `maxHpOf` already reads it).
- `plain: true`: see the shared rule (offer weight `CONFIG.abilities.plainWeight`, validate.js check), as Keen Edge.
- The rim: the HUD health bar draws a 2 px dark iron frame while `kit.mods.maxHp > 0`, thicker by level (1-4 px). HUD only.
- The veins: drawing only, on the existing `abilityPicked` event when its id is this one.

## Multiplayer

Unchanged: each client owns its own health and the server reads the bar from the kit. The rim shows on the holder's own bar; the veins are drawn only in the holder's browser (the pick happens between fights). It touches no teammate.

## Effect

Layered, timed from the pick (t = 0, the `abilityPicked` event, after the pick screen closes):

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00-0.50 | Veins | A branching vein decal on the player's forearm (one pooled decal plane on the arm bone), drawn in flat dark strokes, growing outward from the wrist | `#4a4740` veins, `#16130f` outline |
| 0.05-0.30 | Sparks | 6 short bone-white spark streaks off the forearm, falling | `#f4f1e8` |
| 0.50-1.00 | Cool | The veins fade back to skin | `#4a4740` to transparent |
| from 0.00 | Rim | The health bar gains its iron frame (HUD, held for the run) | `#4a4740` frame, `#8c877b` top highlight |

Budget (Common class): 1 pooled mesh (the decal), 6 particles (3 on Normal), no light, no ribbon, no impact frame. Peak 0.5 s. Reduced motion: no change needed (no flash).

## Sound

`abilityClank` (new, in `js/data/audio.js`; Grit reuses it): a metallic transient (band-passed noise at 1.2 kHz, 25 ms, driven), a body of a low iron ring (sine 180 Hz with a 2.76× partial, decaying over 0.35 s), a short tail (verb 0.3). Played once at the pick, 0.1 s after `abilityPick`.

## Camera

No camera kick: commons never take one.

## Images

- `img/iron-blood-1.webp`: close on the swordsman's gauntleted forearm, dark iron-grey veins spreading under the skin like cooling metal, bone-white sparks.

pool.md:
# Light Step

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Id | `light-step` |
| Rarity | Common (bone ink `#cfc8b6`), 4 levels |
| Kind | Mods (a plain number) |
| Trigger | None: always on (no `when`; raises the `dashRefill` mod) |
| Origin | Kept from js/data/abilities.js: same numbers and text; gains `plain: true`, the refill chime and the heel feather. |

## Card

**Dashes refill {dashRefill} faster.** (4 words, 23 chars; level I reads "Dashes refill 12% faster.")

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): keep the current `ABILITY_ICONS['light-step']`, a feather with two speed strokes.
- Hover loop (1.5 s): one stroke: three short bars, the last one empty (0.2 s), it refills (0.5 s) and a small feather stroke flicks off below it (0.3 s); hold, fade.

## Idea

Faster dash refill: the newcomer's favourite, because every dash is a mistake you get to undo. Three charges come back one at a time over 1.3 s each; this makes the wait shorter. Its touch tells you the moment a charge is back without looking at the HUD: a soft chime, and a single feather of bone ink flicks off the heel.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'light-step', name: 'Light Step', rarity: 'common', plain: true,
  text: 'Dashes refill {dashRefill} faster.', mods: true,
  levels: [{ dashRefill: 0.12 }, { dashRefill: 0.24 }, { dashRefill: 0.36 }, { dashRefill: 0.48 }] },
```

Numbers: a charge comes back in 1.3 s; level I makes it 1.16 s, level IV 0.88 s. Under pressure that is about one extra dash 11 s at level I and about every 3 s at level IV. It never adds a fourth charge, so it softens mistakes without making the dash endless (Last Breath, a rare, does that).

## Engine work

- None for the number: `dashRefill` is an existing `ABILITY_MODS` key (`Player` refill, js/player.js).
- `plain: true`: the shared rule (offer weight, validate.js check), as Keen Edge.
- The chime and feather: the `Player` emits a new `dashReady` event `{ body }` when `dashes` crosses a whole number upward (drawing and audio listen; it never changes state). Played only while the holder has the mod, so a plain player's dash stays silent.

## Multiplayer

Unchanged: each client owns its own movement and dash charges. The feather is drawn by every browser from the holder's pose (it reads their kit); the chime is the holder's alone. It touches no teammate.

## Effect

Layered, timed from each `dashReady` (t = 0):

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00 | Feather | One flat ink-feather stroke flicks from the back heel, a curved blade of ink with a white spine, dark outline | `#cfc8b6` body, `#f4f1e8` spine, `#16130f` outline |
| 0.00-0.30 | Flick | It lifts 0.4 m back and up, turning half a turn, scaling 1.0 to 0.6 | as above |
| 0.20-0.45 | Fade | It fades out | to transparent |

Budget (Common class): 1 pooled mesh (a small pool of 3 feathers so three charges never wait), 0 particles, no light, no ribbon, no impact frame. Peak 0.3 s. Reduced motion: the feather fades in place without turning.

## Sound

`abilityChime` (new, in `js/data/audio.js`): a soft transient tick (high-passed noise at 6 kHz, 10 ms), a body of a small chime (sine 1320 Hz with a 2.76× partial, decaying 0.15 s), no tail. Quiet (vel 0.35), the holder's only. A charge returns at most once every 0.88 s, so it never rings as a run.

## Camera

No camera kick: commons never take one.

## Images

- `img/light-step-1.webp`: the swordsman landing from a dash, three slim white bars of light at their feet refilling, a single ink-brush feather flicking off the heel.

# Quick Draught

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Id | `quick-draught` |
| Rarity | Common (bone ink `#cfc8b6`), 4 levels |
| Kind | Mods (a plain number) |
| Trigger | None: always on (no `when`; raises the `flaskSpeed` mod) |
| Origin | Kept from js/data/abilities.js: same numbers and text; gains `plain: true`, the flask flare and the gulp. |

## Card

**Drink flasks {flaskSpeed} faster.** (4 words, 22 chars; level I reads "Drink flasks 20% faster.")

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): keep the current `ABILITY_ICONS['quick-draught']`, a round flask with three speed lines on its left.
- Hover loop (1.3 s): one stroke: a flask tips up (0.3 s), its level drops in one quick step (0.2 s), a short smear line beside it (0.2 s); hold, fade.

## Idea

Faster flasks, kept small on purpose (Aleix: flask picks made runs too easy). A flask is drunk on the move in 0.95 s and a landed blow cuts it short, so drinking faster is drinking safer: less time slowed, fewer flasks wasted. Its touch: the flask flares warm amber for an instant and a quick gulp, so the faster drink reads as a decision, not a slower animation played fast.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'quick-draught', name: 'Quick Draught', rarity: 'common', plain: true,
  text: 'Drink flasks {flaskSpeed} faster.', mods: true,
  levels: [{ flaskSpeed: 0.2 }, { flaskSpeed: 0.35 }, { flaskSpeed: 0.5 }, { flaskSpeed: 0.6 }] },
```

Numbers: a drink takes 0.95 s; level I makes it 0.79 s, level IV 0.59 s. The heal (45) is unchanged, so it never adds health, only shortens the window a boss can punish. The levels grow by less each step (20, 15, 15, 10) so level IV stays above half the drink time.

## Engine work

- None for the number: `flaskSpeed` is an existing `ABILITY_MODS` key (`Player.drinkRate`).
- `plain: true`: the shared rule (offer weight, validate.js check), as Keen Edge.
- The flare: drawing only, on the existing `itemUsed` event for the flask when the user holds the mod.

## Multiplayer

Unchanged: each client owns its own drinking; the server sees the drinking pose (`PS.USE_ITEM`) as before. The flare is drawn by every browser on that player's flask. It touches no teammate.

## Effect

Layered, timed from the drink's start (t = 0, `itemUsed`):

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00-0.12 | Flare | A small hard-edged four-point glint sprite on the flask in the off hand (the flask has no glow of its own today), held 0.06 s, then fading | `#e8b56a` warm amber body, `#f4f1e8` core |
| 0.00-0.25 | Smear | One bone-ink motion smear arcs round the flask from hip to mouth, a flat curved stroke with a dark outline | `#cfc8b6` body, `#16130f` outline |

Budget (Common class): 2 pooled meshes (the glint sprite, the smear), 0 particles, no light, no ribbon, no impact frame. Peak 0.25 s. Reduced motion: no change needed (one glint a drink, far under 3 Hz).

## Sound

`abilityGulp` (new, in `js/data/audio.js`): a soft low transient (sine 160 Hz, 40 ms), a body of one quick swallow (band-passed noise 400 to 700 Hz, 0.12 s), no tail. Played 0.05 s after the existing `flask` sound, the holder's only.

## Camera

No camera kick: commons never take one.

## Images

- `img/quick-draught-1.webp`: the swordsman drinking from a small glowing amber flask while running, a quick bone-ink motion smear around the flask.

pool.md:
# Breaker

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Id | `breaker` |
| Rarity | Common (bone ink `#cfc8b6`), 4 levels |
| Kind | Mods (a plain number) |
| Trigger | None: always on (no `when`; raises the `counterWindow` mod) |
| Origin | Kept from js/data/abilities.js: same numbers and text; gains `plain: true` and the bone tail on the counter glow. |

## Card

**Counter window {counterWindow} longer.** (4 words, 24 chars; level I reads "Counter window 15% longer.")

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): keep the current `ABILITY_ICONS['breaker']`, a circle split by a jagged crack.
- Hover loop (1.6 s): one stroke: a blade line lights (0.1 s) and dims along a bar beneath it (0.8 s), the bar's last stretch drawn in a paler tone; hold, fade.

## Idea

A longer counter window. The counter is the skill the whole fight turns on, and PLAN asks the picks that used to feed posture to feed counters instead. For a newcomer, the window after a perfect dodge (0.8 s) or a last-blow deflect (1.1 s) is often over before they have turned round; this buys them the turn. Its touch shows the time it bought: the blade's counter glow already dims over the window, and the stretch Breaker added is drawn as a bone-white tail, so you see when you are living on borrowed time.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'breaker', name: 'Breaker', rarity: 'common', plain: true,
  text: 'Counter window {counterWindow} longer.', mods: true,
  levels: [{ counterWindow: 0.15 }, { counterWindow: 0.3 }, { counterWindow: 0.45 }, { counterWindow: 0.6 }] },
```

Numbers: after a perfect dodge the window is 0.8 s (level I 0.92 s, level IV 1.28 s); after a deflect 1.1 s (level I 1.27 s, level IV 1.76 s). It adds no damage; it turns missed counters into landed ones. If one counter in six was missed for want of time, level I recovers about one counter a fight (about 40 damage plus a guard crack toward the Finishing Blow).

## Engine work

- None for the number: `counterWindow` is an existing `ABILITY_MODS` key (js/player.js opens the window, the server's riposte check reads it too).
- `plain: true`: the shared rule (offer weight, validate.js check), as Keen Edge.
- The tail: `counterGlow` (js/player-pose.js) already dims the glow over the window's full length. It also mixes toward bone white once the time left is under the share Breaker added (`riposte < cwFull × counterWindow / (1 + counterWindow)`). Drawing only.

## Multiplayer

Unchanged: the window is the holder's own and the server's riposte check already reads `counterWindow`. The glow is drawn by every browser on that player's blade. It touches no teammate.

## Effect

Layered, timed from the counter window opening (t = 0, `counterOpen`), lasting the window's length `W`:

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00 to W × 1/(1 + counterWindow) | Glow | The existing counter glow on the blade, dimming as now | the existing glow |
| the rest of W | Tail | The same glow, its colour mixed to bone white with a thin dark ink edge on the blade trail, still dimming | `#f4f1e8` core, `#cfc8b6` edge |
| W to W + 0.2 | Out | The tail fades out | to transparent |

Budget (Common class): 0 new meshes (the existing blade glow, recoloured), 0 particles, no light, no ribbon, no impact frame. Peak: none of its own; the tail lasts 0.12-0.66 s by level and window, a recolour of the existing glow rather than a new effect. Reduced motion: no change needed (a colour shift, no flash).

## Sound

None new. The window's own `counterOpen` ring announces it; a sound cannot show the remaining time as clearly as the glow does.

## Camera

No camera kick: commons never take one.

## Images

- `img/breaker-1.webp`: the swordsman after a perfect dodge, the blade glowing with a long, slowly fading white aura while the boss recovers, time feeling stretched.

pool.md:
# Keen Eye

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Id | `keen-eye` |
| Rarity | Common (bone ink `#cfc8b6`), 4 levels |
| Kind | Mods (a plain number) |
| Trigger | None: always on (no `when`; raises the `parryWindow` mod) |
| Origin | Kept from js/data/abilities.js: same numbers and text; gains `plain: true` and the window ring. |

## Card

**Deflect window {parryWindow} wider.** (4 words, 23 chars; level I reads "Deflect window 15% wider.")

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): keep the current `ABILITY_ICONS['keen-eye']`, an eye with three short rays above it.
- Hover loop (1.4 s): one stroke: a blade line falls toward a small figure (0.5 s), a thin ring flickers once round the figure's feet (0.15 s), the figure's guard line flashes (0.1 s); hold, fade.

## Idea

A wider deflect window, for friends new to the genre. The deflect is about a third of a second wide; this widens both of its edges. Its touch teaches the timing: a thin bone ring flickers once round your feet the moment a blow you can deflect comes into your window, so a newcomer learns what "now" looks like, and a veteran can ignore it.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'keen-eye', name: 'Keen Eye', rarity: 'common', plain: true,
  text: 'Deflect window {parryWindow} wider.', mods: true,
  levels: [{ parryWindow: 0.15 }, { parryWindow: 0.3 }, { parryWindow: 0.45 }, { parryWindow: 0.6 }] },
```

Numbers: the window opens 0.13 s before a blow's active frame and closes 0.05 s into it, plus the press's 0.17 s arm: about 0.35 s. Each level widens the lead and grace by its share: level I adds about 0.03 s, level IV about 0.11 s (about 0.46 s in all). Deflects are 6-15 a fight; if one in five was mistimed by a hair, level I saves one or two blows a fight and turns them into key charge and counters.

## Engine work

- None for the number: `parryWindow` is an existing `ABILITY_MODS` key (`parryTiming`, js/combat.js; the server's parry check reads it too).
- `plain: true`: the shared rule (offer weight, validate.js check), as Keen Edge.
- The ring: drawing only, on the local player. Each step, for the locked or nearest enemy in a wind-up, the first step `parryTiming(p, e, 0)` returns a number for a new blow (`blowKey`) draws one ring. At most one ring every 0.4 s (`VIS.abilityFx.small.windowRing.gap`), so a fast string never flickers over 3 Hz.

## Multiplayer

Unchanged: each client owns its own defence and the server's parry check already reads `parryWindow`. The ring is the holder's alone (drawn only in their browser; teammates never see a cue for blows not aimed at them). It touches no teammate.

## Effect

Layered, timed from the blow entering the window (t = 0):

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00 | Ring | A thin flat ring on the ground round the player's feet (radius 0.9 m, 3 cm line), hard edge, a dark ink line just outside it | `#f4f1e8` line, `#cfc8b6` edge, `#16130f` ink line |
| 0.00-0.15 | Hold | Held at full strength while the press would land | as above |
| 0.15-0.35 | Fade | It widens 10% and fades | to transparent |

Budget (Common class): 1 pooled mesh (the ring, the existing `groundFx.ring` pool), 0 particles, no light, no ribbon, no impact frame. Peak 0.15 s. Reduced motion: no widening; the ring fades in place. Never more than one ring every 0.4 s.

## Sound

None. A sound on every boss blow would be noise and would compete with the boss's own tells.

## Camera

No camera kick: commons never take one.

## Images

- `img/keen-eye-1.webp`: the swordsman raising the blade to deflect a huge falling blow, a thin bone-white ring of focus around them, the moment just before impact.

pool.md:
# Cold Riposte

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Id | `cold-riposte` |
| Rarity | Common (bone ink `#cfc8b6`), 4 levels |
| Kind | Mods (a plain number) |
| Trigger | None: always on (no `when`; raises the `riposte` mod, read on every counter) |
| Origin | Kept from js/data/abilities.js: same numbers; text "Ripostes:" becomes "Counters:" (the word the players see, as Riptide's and Pyre's cards); gains `plain: true` and the frost line. |

## Card

**Counters: {riposte} more damage.** (4 words, 24 chars; level I reads "Counters: 15% more damage.")

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): keep the current `ABILITY_ICONS['cold-riposte']`, a sword laid flat with a snowflake above it.
- Hover loop (1.6 s): one stroke: a figure sidesteps (0.3 s), cuts back (0.2 s), the cut line stays and grows small frost ticks along it (0.4 s), which flake away (0.3 s); hold, fade.

## Idea

Counters hit harder. The counter is the skill the fight is about, so this is the plain number that rewards the right thing: it does nothing for a player who only trades blows. Its touch: frost rime crusts along the counter's cut line and flakes away, so every counter you land reads as colder and heavier than a plain blow.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'cold-riposte', name: 'Cold Riposte', rarity: 'common', plain: true,
  text: 'Counters: {riposte} more damage.', mods: true,
  levels: [{ riposte: 0.15 }, { riposte: 0.3 }, { riposte: 0.45 }, { riposte: 0.6 }] },
```

- The frost line: drawing only, on the existing counter cut (js/counter-fx.js draws a thin line where an attack with `cut` lands as a riposte). For a holder of the mod, that line gets a frost crust layer. A counter from an attack without `cut` gets a short crust line of its own across the struck body, along the swing.

## Multiplayer

# Spark Step

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Id | `spark-step` |
| Rarity | Common (bone ink `#cfc8b6`), 4 levels |
| Kind | Triggered power (no key) |
| Trigger | `dashPast` (new): a dash that passes close by or through an enemy's body and carries on past it |
| Origin | New |

## Card

**Dash past the boss: a spark cuts it.** (8 words, 36 chars)

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): a zigzag line running across the box, with a small four-point star where it crosses a circle.
- Hover loop (1.4 s): a small figure dashes past a circle (0.3 s), a zigzag line draws itself along the path behind it (0.2 s) and snaps into a star on the circle (0.1 s); hold, fade.

## Idea

Dashing close past or through the boss leaves a crackling line on the ground that snaps shut on it. The safe dash goes away from the boss; this rewards the brave one, through its legs or round its flank, which is also how you get behind it for a counter. Each such dash becomes a small hit, so a player who moves well deals damage just by moving.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'spark-step', name: 'Spark Step', rarity: 'common',
  text: 'Dash past the boss: a spark cuts it.',
  power: { when: 'dashPast', then: 'spark' },
  levels: [
    { damage: 10, cooldown: 1 },
    { damage: 13, cooldown: 1 },
    { damage: 16, cooldown: 1 },
    { damage: 19, cooldown: 1 },
  ] },
```

Numbers: a light hit is 16, so a spark is about two thirds of one. A player who dashes past the boss 8-15 times a fight (the 1 s cooldown stops dash-spam inside a flurry) deals about 80-150 more at level I and 150-285 at level IV: level with Keen Edge, but only for the dashes that take the risk.

## Engine work

- New `when: 'dashPast'`: fired once at the end of a dash whose path (the segment from where it began to where it ended) came within `CONFIG.abilities.commons.pastGap` (1.2 m) of a live enemy's body edge, with the closest point strictly between the ends (it went past, not into). `ctx`: `{ enemy, from: { x, z }, to: { x, z } }`, the nearest such enemy. A dash that passes nothing fires nothing and spends no cooldown.
- Reuses `then: 'spark'` (Static Edge's resolver: `damage` to that enemy, as a power's blow). `ABILITY_POWERS['dashPast/spark'] = ['damage', 'cooldown']`.
- Drawing: ability-fx.js's `spark` today draws Static Edge's short blue bolt. A `spark` event with a `path` (copied from `ctx.from/to` into the `abilityPower` event) is drawn as the zigzag along it, in the colour of the ability's rarity (`picked[rarity]`), never by its id.
- Shared by the effect commons: validate.js's kind rule becomes "`mods` only on a common, `perk` on a common or a rare, `power` on any rarity"; camera-feel.js skips `abilityPerk`/`abilityPower` events whose ability is a common.
- `validate.js`: `dashPast/spark` needs `damage` and `cooldown` (the existing plan check).

## Multiplayer

A person's dash is theirs, so `dashPast` joins `ABILITY_CLAIMS`: the browser claims it with the enemy and the path; the server checks the player's poses showed a dash in the last 0.5 s, that the claimed path starts and ends within 1.5 m of those poses, and that the enemy's body was within `pastGap` + 0.5 m of it, then resolves the spark. It hits enemies only; a teammate on the path sees the line pass through them. Everyone sees the line.

## Effect

Layered, timed from the dash's end (t = 0):

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00 | Line | A flat zigzag strip on the ground along the dash path (a ground-hugging quad stretched start to end, zigzag texture, 0.25 m wide), hard white core, bone edge, dark ink outline | `#f4f1e8` core, `#cfc8b6` edge, `#16130f` outline |
| 0.00-0.08 | Draw | It draws itself from the start of the path to its end | as above |
| 0.08-0.14 | Snap | At the point nearest the enemy, a small four-point star (0.6 m) snaps open on the enemy's flank at waist height | `#f4f1e8` core, `#cfc8b6` points |
| 0.08-0.30 | Sparks | 12 short hard spark streaks thrown off the star | `#f4f1e8` heads, `#8c877b` tails |
| 0.20-0.50 | Fade | Line and star fade, the line from its start | to transparent |

Budget (Common class): 2 pooled meshes (the line strip, the star sprite), 12 particles (7 on Normal), no light, no ribbon, no impact frame. Peak 0.14 s. Reduced motion: the line appears whole instead of drawing on; no other flash to soften. At most one a second (the cooldown).

## Sound

Reuse `abilitySpark` (Static Edge's: a hard high crack, a short FM buzz, a fizz) at pitch 1.15 and vel 0.6, played at the snap: the same sound family, lighter, so a rare's spark still sounds bigger.

## Camera

No camera kick: commons never take one. The existing `powers.spark` entry is Static Edge's; camera-feel.js skips it for a common's spark.

## Images

- `img/spark-step-1.webp`: the swordsman dashing past a towering boss in a blur, a crackling zigzag line of bone-white electricity drawn along the dash path snapping on the boss.

# Ringing Steel

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Id | `ringing-steel` |
| Rarity | Common (bone ink `#cfc8b6`), 4 levels |
| Kind | Triggered perk (no key) |
| Trigger | `parry`: the holder deflects a blow |
| Origin | New |

## Card

**Deflect: your next dash is free.** (6 words, 32 chars)

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): two crossed blade strokes with two concentric arcs ringing out from the cross, and a short dash arrow beneath.
- Hover loop (1.6 s): a blade line meets a falling blow (0.1 s), two rings spread from the clash (0.4 s), the figure dashes away leaving a faint ringing trail (0.4 s); hold, fade.

## Idea

Each deflect rings and banks a free dash. The deflect leaves you face to face with the boss; the free dash is the way round it to its back for the counter, even with your charges spent. It ties the two defences together: deflect, then dash, and the dash costs nothing. The ring you see and hear is the reminder that one is banked.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'ringing-steel', name: 'Ringing Steel', rarity: 'common',
  text: 'Deflect: your next dash is free.',
  perk: { when: 'parry', then: 'freeDash' },
  levels: [{ cooldown: 6 }, { cooldown: 5 }, { cooldown: 4 }, { cooldown: 3 }] },
```

Numbers: a charge comes back in 1.3 s, so a free dash is worth about 1.3 s of refill, and it matters most at zero charges, when it is the only dash there is. At most one bank every 6 s at level I (about 10 a fight if you deflect that often) and every 3 s at level IV. Banks never stack past one.

## Engine work

- Reuses the perk `when: 'parry'` (Iron Mercy's) and the `freeDash` effect (Last Breath's `low/freeDash`). New pair `ABILITY_PERKS['parry/freeDash'] = ['cooldown']`.
- Perk clocks (`abilityPerkState`): `freeDash` (0 or 1, a banked dash) and `ring` (s until it may bank again). A deflect with `ring` at 0 sets `freeDash = 1` and `ring = cooldown`; `abilityClocks` counts `ring` down.
- `Player.freeDash()` also returns true while `perk.freeDash` is 1, and the dash that uses it spends the bank instead of a charge (js/player.js line 151): so `canRoll` allows a dash at zero charges. The bank is cleared at the fight's end.
- Emits `abilityPerk` `{ perk: 'parry/freeDash' }` on banking and `{ perk: 'freeDash/spent' }` when the dash uses it (drawing and audio listen).
- Shared by the effect commons: the validate.js kind rule and the camera-feel.js common skip (see Spark Step).

## Multiplayer

A perk on the holder's own body: their browser runs it (each client owns its movement and dashes). The server needs nothing: it never checks dash charges. It moves only its holder. The ring and the trail are drawn in the holder's browser only, as every perk cue is today (`abilityPerk` is the local player's); teammates see the deflect's own spark.

## Effect

Layered, timed from the deflect (t = 0); the trail plays on the free dash itself (t' = 0):

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00 | Ring | A clear flat ring of sound, upright, centred on the clash point and facing the attacker: two hard thin concentric rings, white core lines with bone edges, a dark ink line outside the outer one | `#f4f1e8` lines, `#cfc8b6` edge, `#16130f` ink |
| 0.00-0.35 | Spread | Both rings expand from 0.3 m to 1.6 m, the inner a beat behind, thinning | as above |
| 0.25-0.45 | Fade | They fade out | to transparent |
| t' 0.00-0.40 | Trail | On the free dash: the dash's existing afterimages tinted bone, and a faint ring shape left at the start of the dash, fading | `#cfc8b6`, `#8c877b` |

Budget (Common class): 2 pooled meshes (the two rings; the trail reuses js/afterimage.js's pooled figures, tinted, and one of the rings), 0 particles, no light, no ribbon, no impact frame. Peak 0.35 s. Reduced motion: the rings fade in place without spreading.

## Sound

`abilityRing` (new, in `js/data/audio.js`): no hard transient (the deflect's own clash is the hit), a body of a clear bell partial (sine 1760 Hz with partials at 1.5× and 2.76×, decaying over 0.6 s), a tail of a short room (verb 0.45). On the free dash it plays again at pitch 0.9, vel 0.35, the holder's only.

## Camera

No camera kick: commons never take one (the deflect has its own). camera-feel.js's `perkFov` skips this common's `abilityPerk`.

## Images

- `img/ringing-steel-1.webp`: the swordsman deflecting a blow with a bright clash, a crisp ring of sound waves expanding from the blade, then dashing away leaving an echoing trail.

**Perfect dodge: your afterimage strikes once.** (6 words, 44 chars)

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): a dashed outline of a figure with a single curved slash stroke in front of it, and a solid figure stepping away to the side.
- Hover loop (1.6 s): a figure sidesteps a falling blow (0.3 s), the dashed outline left behind swings one slash (0.2 s) and breaks into flakes (0.3 s); hold, fade.

## Idea

The perfect dodge already leaves an afterimage where you stood; Echo Step makes it swing once at the boss before it fades. The dodge itself hits back, so the boss is punished for the blow you slipped even before your counter lands. It reads as one clean beat: you are already gone, and the copy you left still cuts.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'echo-step', name: 'Echo Step', rarity: 'common',
  text: 'Perfect dodge: your afterimage strikes once.',
  power: { when: 'dodge', then: 'afterimage' },
  levels: [{ damage: 14 }, { damage: 18 }, { damage: 22 }, { damage: 26 }] },
```

Numbers: a light hit is 16, so the afterimage's cut is a light hit at level I and over one and a half at level IV. Perfect dodges come 6-12 times a fight: about 85-170 more at level I and 155-310 at level IV. No cooldown: a perfect dodge is earned each time. It never opens a counter of its own and never cracks a guard (a power's blow is never a counter).

## Engine work

- Reuses `when: 'dodge'` (Time Rift's and Counterstep's).
- New `then: 'afterimage'`: 0.15 s after the dodge (`CONFIG.abilities.commons.imageDelay`), `damage` to the dodged enemy if its body is within `CONFIG.abilities.commons.imageReach` (2.8 m) of where the holder stood when the blow met them (`ctx.x/z`, the dodge point), as a power's blow. Out of reach, nothing. Runs as a `running` entry (one strike, `next` = the delay), like a twin's echo. Add it to `ON_ENEMY`. `ABILITY_POWERS['dodge/afterimage'] = ['damage']`.
- Drawing: js/afterimage.js already leaves a brighter, longer copy on a perfect dodge. A new `afterimage` case in ability-fx.js poses that copy's figure in the swing (the `light` attack's active pose), turned to the enemy, and draws the slash and the flakes.
- Shared by the effect commons: the validate.js kind rule and the camera-feel.js common skip (see Spark Step).

## Multiplayer

The perfect dodge is already a claim (`ABILITY_CLAIMS` has `dodge`; the server checks a blow of that attack was out near the player). The claim adds the dodge point; the server checks it within 1.5 m of the player's pose at that time and the enemy within `imageReach` of it, then resolves the cut. It hits that enemy only. Everyone sees the copy swing.

## Effect

Layered, timed from the perfect dodge (t = 0):

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00 | Copy | The perfect dodge's afterimage, recoloured as a flat grey ink silhouette with a dark outline, where the holder stood | `#8c877b` body, `#cfc8b6` rim, `#16130f` outline |
| 0.08-0.18 | Swing | The copy snaps into the light swing's active pose, turned to the enemy | as above |
| 0.15-0.30 | Slash | One flat brush-stroke crescent (1.4 m) along the swing, dry-brush ends, white core | `#f4f1e8` core, `#cfc8b6` edge, `#16130f` ends |
| 0.25-0.55 | Flakes | The copy dissolves into 16 hard-edged ink flakes drifting back and down | `#4a4740`, `#16130f`, a few `#cfc8b6` |

Budget (Common class): 2 pooled meshes (the copy, which is js/afterimage.js's pooled figure; the slash), 16 particles (9 on Normal), no light, no ribbon, no impact frame. Peak 0.15 s at the slash. Reduced motion: no change needed (no flash); the copy fades instead of flaking.

## Sound

Reuse `abilityEcho` (the ember twin's echoed blow) at pitch 1.2 and vel 0.55, played at the slash: a lighter echo of a cut.

## Camera

No camera kick: commons never take one (the perfect dodge has its slow beat).

## Images

- `img/echo-step-1.webp`: the swordsman dodging aside while a grey ink afterimage of them, left behind, swings a brush-stroke slash at the boss and flakes away.

# Petal Cut

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Id | `petal-cut` |
| Rarity | Common (bone ink `#cfc8b6`), 4 levels |
| Kind | Triggered power (no key) |
| Trigger | `dashStrike` (new): a dash attack (the light or heavy a dash turns into) lands on an enemy, unblocked |
| Origin | New |

## Card

**Dash attack: the cut opens again a beat later.** (9 words, 46 chars)

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): a straight cut line across the box with a short dash arrow behind it, splitting open in the middle with three small petal shapes.
- Hover loop (1.6 s): a figure dashes through a shape (0.3 s), a thin line stays across it (0.35 s, still), then splits open and three petals drift off (0.4 s); hold, fade.

## Idea

The dash attack's cut line hangs in the air and opens a second time a beat later: the delayed cut, the signature of the game's blade techniques, in miniature. It makes the dash attack, the fastest way in, worth a little more, and it teaches the look the bigger techniques use (a line that hangs, then opens), so the counter's and the Finishing Blow's cuts read at once.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'petal-cut', name: 'Petal Cut', rarity: 'common',
  text: 'Dash attack: the cut opens again a beat later.',
  power: { when: 'dashStrike', then: 'lateCut' },
  levels: [{ damage: 12 }, { damage: 15 }, { damage: 18 }, { damage: 21 }] },
```

Numbers: a dash light does 22 and a dash heavy 34, so the late cut adds about half of a dash light at level I. Dash attacks land 6-12 times a fight: about 70-145 more at level I and 125-250 at level IV. No cooldown: the dash spaces it.

## Engine work

- New `when: 'dashStrike'`: a blow of one of the moveset's dash attacks (`PLAYER_DEF.moveset.dash`, the pair `dashAttackFrom` already chooses between) lands unblocked. `ctx`: `{ enemy, strike }`.
- New `then: 'lateCut'`: `CONFIG.abilities.commons.lateCut` (0.35 s) later, `damage` to that enemy if it is still alive and can be hurt, as a power's blow. A `running` entry (one strike, `next` = the delay), like a twin's echo. Add it to `ON_ENEMY`. `ABILITY_POWERS['dashStrike/lateCut'] = ['damage']`.
- Drawing: js/counter-fx.js already hangs a thin line where a counter with `cut` lands and opens it `cut.open` s later. A new `lateCut` case in ability-fx.js uses the same pooled cut sprites: the line at the dash attack's hit, opened on the late cut's own `abilityPower` event (the `strike` event, so the opening is drawn when the damage lands).
- Shared by the effect commons: the validate.js kind rule and the camera-feel.js common skip (see Spark Step).

## Multiplayer

The server sees every landed blow with its attack id, so no claim: in `Simulation.hit`, a landed dash attack triggers `dashStrike` for the striker; the server runs the delay and resolves the late cut. It hits that enemy only. Everyone sees the line and its opening.

## Effect

Layered, timed from the dash attack's hit (t = 0); the late cut lands at t = 0.35:

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00 | Line | A thin straight cut line across the enemy along the thrust (1.6 m, 2 cm), hard white core, bone edge, held perfectly still in the air | `#f4f1e8` core, `#cfc8b6` edge |
| 0.00-0.35 | Hang | Held, a faint dark ink shadow line beside it | `#16130f` shadow |
| 0.35-0.45 | Open | The line splits open into a narrow lens (0.12 m wide at its middle), brighter for 0.05 s | `#f4f1e8`, `#cfc8b6` edge |
| 0.35-0.60 | Petals | 6 pale flat petals (hard-edged, two-tone) slip out of the opening and drift down, turning | `#ece6d8` face, `#8c877b` shade side |
| 0.45-0.60 | Fade | The lens closes and fades | to transparent |

Budget (Common class): 1 pooled mesh (the cut sprite, counter-fx.js's pool), 6 particles (3 on Normal), no light, no ribbon, no impact frame. Peak 0.1 s at the opening. Reduced motion: no brightening at the opening; the line widens and fades.

## Sound

Reuse `cutOpen` (the counter's cut opening) at pitch 1.3 and vel 0.45, played at the opening: the same family as the bigger delayed cuts, smaller.

## Camera

No camera kick: commons never take one.

# Thorn Guard

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Id | `thorn-guard` |
| Rarity | Common (bone ink `#cfc8b6`), 4 levels |
| Kind | Triggered power (no key) |
| Trigger | `block`: an enemy's blow lands on the holder's raised guard |
| Origin | New |

## Card

**Block: thorns hit the attacker.** (5 words, 31 chars)

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): a round shield face-on with four short sharp thorn strokes jutting out of it to the right.
- Hover loop (1.4 s): a blow falls on a round shield (0.3 s), thorn strokes jab out toward the attacker (0.1 s) and pull back (0.2 s); hold, fade.

## Idea

A blocked blow drives black ink thorns out of the shield into the attacker. Blocking is the newcomer's first defence and today it is only waiting; with this it answers. It never replaces the deflect (a deflect opens a counter and fills the keys far more), it only makes the safe choice less passive.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'thorn-guard', name: 'Thorn Guard', rarity: 'common',
  text: 'Block: thorns hit the attacker.',
  power: { when: 'block', then: 'thorns' },
  levels: [
    { damage: 8, cooldown: 0.8 },
    { damage: 11, cooldown: 0.8 },
    { damage: 14, cooldown: 0.8 },
    { damage: 17, cooldown: 0.8 },
  ] },
```

Numbers: half a light hit at level I, a light hit at level IV. A player who blocks takes 8-16 blows on the guard a fight: about 65-130 more at level I and 135-270 at level IV. The 0.8 s cooldown stops a fast string from firing it on every blow. A blocked blow still costs 15% of its damage, so it never makes blocking better than deflecting.

## Engine work

- `when: 'block'` exists as a perk trigger (Bastion's `block/charge`); a power on it is new. `Player.takeHit` already knows a blow was blocked; it calls `abilityReport(this, 'block', { enemy: attacker })` when the attacker is an enemy whose body is within `CONFIG.abilities.commons.thornReach` (3.5 m) of the holder's (a blocked bolt from afar fires nothing and spends no cooldown).
- New `then: 'thorns'`: `damage` to that enemy as a power's blow (the `flare`/`spark` case in `fire`). Add it to `ON_ENEMY`. `ABILITY_POWERS['block/thorns'] = ['damage', 'cooldown']`.
- Drawing: a new `thorns` case in ability-fx.js on the holder's shield, aimed at the enemy.
- Shared by the effect commons: the validate.js kind rule and the camera-feel.js common skip (see Spark Step).

## Multiplayer

Each client owns its defence, so a block is seen only in the blocker's browser: `block` joins `ABILITY_CLAIMS`. The claim names the enemy and its blow (`serial`, `hit`); the server checks that blow was out near the player lately (as the dodge claim's `struckNear`), the player's pose was blocking and facing it, and the enemy within `thornReach`, then resolves the thorns. It hits that enemy only. Everyone sees the thorns.

## Effect

Layered, timed from the blocked blow (t = 0):

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00 | Thorns | 3-5 black ink thorns (flat, hard-edged long triangles, 0.5-0.9 m) jab out of the round shield's face toward the attacker, each with a thin bone rim on one edge | `#16130f` body, `#4a4740` shade side, `#cfc8b6` rim |
| 0.00-0.06 | Jab | They shoot out to full length | as above |
| 0.06-0.15 | Hold | Held at full length | as above |
| 0.10-0.20 | Chips | 8 short dark splinter streaks off the thorn tips at the attacker | `#16130f`, `#8c877b` |
| 0.15-0.30 | Retract | They pull back into the shield and fade | to transparent |

Budget (Common class): 1 pooled mesh (one thorn-cluster mesh, its 5 thorns scaled per hit), 8 particles (4 on Normal), no light, no ribbon, no impact frame. Peak 0.15 s. Reduced motion: no change needed (no flash).

## Sound

`abilityThorns` (new, in `js/data/audio.js`): a transient of three dry cracks of wood (band-passed noise at 1.5-3 kHz, 15 ms each, 30 ms apart), a body of a short scrape (band-passed noise at 900 Hz, 0.1 s), no tail. Played just after the block's own sound, vel 0.5.

## Camera

No camera kick: commons never take one.

## Images

- `img/thorn-guard-1.webp`: the swordsman blocking a heavy blow with a round shield, sharp black ink thorns stabbing out of the shield face into the attacker.

# Ash Veil

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Id | `ash-veil` |
| Rarity | Common (bone ink `#cfc8b6`), 4 levels |
| Kind | Triggered perk (no key), once a fight |
| Trigger | `low`: the holder's health falls to or under a third of the bar (`below`) |
| Origin | New |

## Card

**Low health: the next blow does {cut} less.** (8 words, 38 chars; level I reads "Low health: the next blow does 40% less.")

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): a figure outline wrapped in two loose curling strokes, a short falling blade line meeting them.
- Hover loop (1.8 s): a bar drops to a third (0.3 s), two curling strokes wrap the figure (0.4 s), a blow falls and the strokes burst into flakes (0.3 s); hold, fade.

## Idea

Once a fight, falling under a third of your bar wraps you in a veil of grey ash that eats most of the next blow. It is a second chance you can see coming: the veil is on you, so you know you have one blow of grace, and so does a friend watching. It rewards nothing by itself; it buys the time to drink, dash out or land the counter that turns it round.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'ash-veil', name: 'Ash Veil', rarity: 'common',
  text: 'Low health: the next blow does {cut} less.',
  perk: { when: 'low', then: 'veil', once: true },
  levels: [
    { below: 0.33, cut: 0.4 },
    { below: 0.33, cut: 0.5 },
    { below: 0.33, cut: 0.6 },
    { below: 0.33, cut: 0.7 },
  ] },
```

Numbers: a third of 120 is 40; a boss blow is mostly 20-40. Level I takes 8-16 off that one blow, level IV 14-28: often the difference between surviving the follow-up and not. Once a fight, so its whole worth is one blow: a small, clear safety pick, below Iron Blood's level IV but felt at the moment it matters.

## Engine work

- Reuses the perk `when: 'low'` (Last Breath's `low/freeDash`). New `then: 'veil'`: `ABILITY_PERKS['low/veil'] = ['below', 'cut']`.
- New: `once` on a perk (until now only powers had it). validate.js: `perk.once` is `true` or `false`, as `power.once`.
- Perk clocks (`abilityPerkState`): `veil` (0 idle, 1 on, 2 spent this fight). In `abilityHurt`, when health is now at or under `below` and `veil` is 0, set it to 1 and emit `abilityPerk` `{ perk: 'low/veil' }`. In `Player.takeHit`, an enemy's blow while `veil` is 1 does `cut` less (before the block's cut), sets `veil` to 2 and emits `{ perk: 'veil/spent' }`. Falls, burns and ground fire do not spend it. `veil` is 0 again at each fight's start.
- `ABILITY_SHARES` gains `cut` (a share, at most 1).
- Shared by the effect commons: the validate.js kind rule and the camera-feel.js common skip (see Spark Step).

## Multiplayer

A perk on the holder's own body: their browser runs it (each client owns its health and defence). The server needs nothing. It touches no teammate. The veil and its burst are drawn in the holder's browser, as every perk cue is today.

## Effect

Layered: the veil from the moment it arms (t = 0), the burst from the blow (t' = 0):

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00-0.40 | Wrap | A grey ash veil swirls up round the body from the feet: a loose open spiral band (one pooled mesh), flat two-tone ash texture with dark ink edges, 1.8 m tall | `#8c877b` body, `#4a4740` shade, `#cfc8b6` leading edge, `#16130f` ink edge |
| 0.40 on | Hold | It turns slowly round the body (0.3 turns a second) at 45% opacity until the blow | as above |
| t' 0.00 | Burst | The band breaks into 20 flat ash flakes thrown outward from the blow's side, turning | `#8c877b`, `#cfc8b6`, `#16130f` |
| t' 0.00-0.50 | Settle | The flakes slow and drift down, fading | to transparent |

Budget (Common class): 1 pooled mesh (the band), 20 particles (11 on Normal), no light, no ribbon, no impact frame. Peak 0.4 s at the wrap; the held band is a quiet low-opacity aura (its only long layer, kept translucent so it never hides the boss's tells), and the burst lasts 0.5 s. Reduced motion: the band holds still instead of turning.

## Sound

`abilityVeil` (new, in `js/data/audio.js`): on arming, a soft rising whoosh (pink noise, band-passed sweeping 300 to 900 Hz over 0.4 s, vel 0.4); on the blow, a transient soft puff (low-passed noise at 600 Hz, 50 ms), a body of a dusty hiss (high-passed noise at 2 kHz, decaying over 0.4 s), a tail of a short room (verb 0.4). The holder's only.

## Camera

No camera kick: commons never take one. camera-feel.js's `perkFov` skips this common's `abilityPerk`.

## Images

- `img/ash-veil-1.webp`: a wounded swordsman wrapped in a swirling veil of grey ash, a boss blow landing and the veil bursting into flakes that absorb it.

# Bitter Draught

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Id | `bitter-draught` |
| Rarity | Common (bone ink `#cfc8b6`), 4 levels |

| Trigger | `flask`: the holder drinks a flask |
| Origin | New |

## Card

**Flask: your next {hits} hits burn.** (6 words, 29 chars; level I reads "Flask: your next 3 hits burn.")

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): a round flask beside an upright sword with three small flame tongues along its blade.
- Hover loop (1.8 s): a flask tips (0.3 s), three small flames catch along a blade (0.3 s), the blade cuts three times and one flame goes out with each (0.8 s); hold, fade.

## Idea

Drinking a flask lights the blade for a few hits. Healing is the moment a newcomer backs off and loses the thread; this makes it a reason to go straight back in. The flames on the blade are the count: you can see how many burning hits are left without any number on the HUD.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'bitter-draught', name: 'Bitter Draught', rarity: 'common',
  text: 'Flask: your next {hits} hits burn.',
  power: { when: 'flask', then: 'burnHits' },
  levels: [
    { hits: 3, damage: 9 },
    { hits: 4, damage: 9 },
    { hits: 5, damage: 9 },
    { hits: 6, damage: 9 },
  ] },
```

Numbers: each burning hit adds 9 (about half a light hit). A flask lights 3-6 hits: 27-54 per flask. With 2-4 flasks a fight that is about 55-110 more at level I and 110-215 at level IV. A new flask renews the count; it never stacks.

## Engine work

- Reuses `when: 'flask'` (Ember Twin's).
- New `then: 'burnHits'`: sets a count of `hits` burning blows on the holder (perk clocks: `burn`, `burnV`; renewed, not added, by another flask; cleared at the fight's end). Each landed, unblocked blow of the holder's own while `burn` > 0 wounds that enemy for `damage` as a power's blow and counts `burn` down, emitting `abilityPower` with `strike` (its number) for the drawing. `ABILITY_POWERS['flask/burnHits'] = ['hits', 'damage']`.
- `hits` here is a count of blows (unit `n`, whole), as Bloodthirst's.
- Drawing: a new `burnHits` case in ability-fx.js: the flames on the holder's blade, one fewer on each `strike` event.
- Shared by the effect commons: the validate.js kind rule and the camera-feel.js common skip (see Spark Step).

## Multiplayer

The flask is already a claim (`ABILITY_CLAIMS` has `flask`; the server checks the drinking pose). The server keeps the burn count on that person's perk clocks and spends it on the landed blows it sees, so each burn is resolved where the enemies are owned. It hits only the enemies the holder strikes. Everyone sees the flames on that player's blade.

## Effect

Layered, timed from the drink (t = 0); each burning hit at its hit frame (t' = 0):

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00-0.30 | Catch | Small flat flame tongues catch along the blade from hilt to tip, one per burning hit (one pooled strip mesh on the blade, its tongues masked by the count), pale bodies with dark red inner lines, bone edges, dark ink outlines | `#ece2cc` body, `#cfc8b6` edge, `#7a1e14` inner lines, `#16130f` outline |
| 0.30 on | Hold | They flicker gently in shape (no brightness flicker) until spent | as above |
| t' 0.00-0.20 | Burn | On the struck enemy, a small hard-edged flame burst and 6 ember streaks | `#ece2cc` burst, `#7a1e14` streak tails |
| t' 0.00-0.15 | Out | The tongue nearest the tip shrinks and goes out | to transparent |

Budget (Common class): 2 pooled meshes (the blade strip, the burst sprite), 6 particles a hit (3 on Normal), no light, no ribbon, no impact frame. Peak 0.3 s at the catch, 0.2 s a hit. The held flames are small and on the blade only. Reduced motion: the flames hold still in shape.

## Sound

Reuse `abilityFlare` at pitch 1.4 and vel 0.4 when the flames catch (a small whoomp). Each burning hit: `abilitySinge` (new, in `js/data/audio.js`): a short hiss transient (band-passed noise at 3 kHz, 60 ms) and a body of a soft crackle (noise grains at 1-2 kHz over 0.1 s), vel 0.4, under the hit's own sound.

# Grit

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Id | `grit` |
| Rarity | Common (bone ink `#cfc8b6`), 4 levels |
| Kind | Triggered perk (no key) |
| Trigger | `hurt`: the holder loses health to a blow |
| Origin | New |

## Card

**Get hit: take {cut} less for {time}.** (7 words, 27 chars; level I reads "Get hit: take 20% less for 1.5 s.")

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): a figure outline with a short blow line striking its shoulder and two small spark strokes glancing off.
- Hover loop (1.6 s): a blow strikes a figure (0.2 s), the figure's outline thickens to a heavy line (0.1 s), a second blow glances off it with sparks (0.3 s), the outline thins back (0.6 s); hold, fade.

## Idea

After a hit, the skin turns iron grey for a moment, so the boss's follow-up hurts less. Bosses' danger is in combos; a newcomer caught by the first blow usually eats the second too. Grit softens exactly that second blow and shows it: the body goes dull iron and the next blow glances off in sparks.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'grit', name: 'Grit', rarity: 'common',
  text: 'Get hit: take {cut} less for {time}.',
  perk: { when: 'hurt', then: 'ironSkin' },
  levels: [
    { cut: 0.2, time: 1.5 },
    { cut: 0.25, time: 1.5 },
    { cut: 0.3, time: 1.5 },
    { cut: 0.35, time: 1.5 },
  ] },
```

Numbers: a boss's follow-up blow is mostly 20-40, so level I takes 4-8 off it and level IV 7-14. A player caught in 4-8 combos a fight saves about 15-60 health at level I: about one flask's worth at the top end. 1.5 s covers a boss's next blow in a string (most strings space blows 0.3-1 s apart).

## Engine work

- Reuses the perk `when: 'hurt'` (Vengeance's: `abilityHurt` runs on losing health). New `then: 'ironSkin'`: `ABILITY_PERKS['hurt/ironSkin'] = ['cut', 'time']`.
- Perk clocks (`abilityPerkState`): `iron` (s left) and `ironCut`. In `abilityHurt`, when `iron` is 0, set it to `time` (a hit inside the 1.5 s does not renew it, so a long combo is softened once and steady pressure cannot keep it up). `abilityClocks` counts it down. In `Player.takeHit`, an enemy's blow while `iron` > 0 does `cut` less (it stacks multiplicatively with the block's cut). Emits `abilityPerk` `{ perk: 'hurt/ironSkin' }` on starting.
- `ABILITY_SHARES` gains `cut` (a share, at most 1), as Ash Veil.

# Kindling

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Id | `kindling` |
| Rarity | Common (bone ink `#cfc8b6`), 4 levels |
| Kind | Triggered perk (no key) |
| Trigger | `parry`: the holder deflects a blow |
| Origin | New |

## Card

**Deflect: every key gains {charge} charge.** (6 words, 34 chars; level I reads "Deflect: every key gains 1 charge.")

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): a small clash spark at the bottom with four thin lines rising from it to four small squares in a row.
- Hover loop (1.5 s): a blade meets a blow (0.1 s), a spark splits into four threads that rise (0.4 s) to four key caps, each flaring once in turn (0.3 s); hold, fade.

## Idea

Deflects feed the four ability keys more. The keys are where the techniques live, and they fill from playing well; this tilts that toward the deflect, so a player who deflects fires techniques sooner. The spark that leaps from the clash to the key caps on the HUD connects the two in the player's head: deflect, and your technique is nearer.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'kindling', name: 'Kindling', rarity: 'common',
  text: 'Deflect: every key gains {charge} charge.',
  perk: { when: 'parry', then: 'keys' },
  levels: [{ charge: 1 }, { charge: 2 }, { charge: 3 }, { charge: 4 }] },
```

Numbers: a deflect already gives every key 3 points; a rare key needs 12-20 and an Ultimate 36-46. Level I makes a deflect worth 4 (a third more); level IV makes it 7. With 6-15 deflects a fight, level I adds 6-15 points to each key held (about half a rare key), level IV 24-60 (one to three more rare fires). Level IV is strong for a common when the kit holds several keys: watch it in play. It does nothing for a kit with no key ability.

## Engine work

- Reuses the perk `when: 'parry'`. New `then: 'keys'`: `ABILITY_PERKS['parry/keys'] = ['charge']`, run with the existing `abilityGain(kit, st, charge)` on the deflect, after the deflect's own gain. Emits `abilityPerk` `{ perk: 'parry/keys' }` (only when the kit holds a key).
- `charge` here is points, not a key's cost: it shares the name with pressed abilities' `charge` (unit `n`, whole), but a key's cost is read only through `kit.pressed`, which holds only abilities with a `key`, so no clash.
- The HUD: the key caps flare on the `abilityPerk` event (js/hud.js), the held keys only.
- Shared by the effect commons: the validate.js kind rule and the camera-feel.js common skip (see Spark Step).

## Multiplayer

The key charge is counted on both sides: the holder's browser and the server (which checks presses against its own count). The server sees the deflect itself (`Simulation`'s parry claim), so it adds the `charge` to that person's count in the same place it adds `CONFIG.abilities.press.gain.deflect`. It touches no teammate's keys.

## Effect

Layered, timed from the deflect (t = 0):

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00 | Spark | A small hard four-point spark at the clash point (0.4 m) | `#f4f1e8` core, `#cfc8b6` points |
| 0.05-0.40 | Threads (HUD) | On the HUD, from the player's screen position, one thin bone line per held key leaps up and arcs to that key cap, drawn on like a brush stroke | `#cfc8b6` line, `#16130f` hairline edge |
| 0.40-0.60 | Flare (HUD) | Each reached key cap's rim brightens once and settles, the caps 0.05 s apart | `#f4f1e8` to the cap's colour |

Budget (Common class): 1 pooled mesh (the spark sprite; the threads and flares are HUD strokes), 0 particles, no light, no ribbon, no impact frame. Peak 0.2 s at the flares. A string's blows can be deflected 0.3 s apart, so the flares play at most once every 0.4 s (`VIS.abilityFx.small.keysGap`); a deflect inside that gap adds its points without a second flare. Reduced motion: the threads appear whole and fade instead of leaping.

## Sound

`abilityKeys` (new, in `js/data/audio.js`; Tithe reuses it): four quick soft ticks rising (sine blips at 880, 990, 1110 and 1320 Hz, 25 ms each, 40 ms apart), no transient or tail beyond them (vel 0.35, the holder's only), one tick per held key.

## Camera

# Kindred Ember

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Id | `kindred-ember` |
| Rarity | Common (bone ink `#cfc8b6`), 4 levels |
| Kind | Triggered perk (no key), offered only in a party |
| Trigger | `revive` (new): the holder finishes reviving a fallen teammate |
| Origin | New |

## Card

**Revive a friend: they rise with {heal} more health.** (9 words, 46 chars; level I reads "Revive a friend: they rise with 10% more health.")

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): a small ember shape on a ground line with two figure outlines, one kneeling over it, one rising, and a short arc sweeping out from the ember.
- Hover loop (2.0 s): a figure kneels by an ember while a ring fills round it (0.8 s), a second figure rises (0.3 s) and a ring sweeps out from the ember (0.4 s); hold, fade.

## Idea

The co-op common: a friend you revive gets up stronger. Reviving is the most generous thing a player does in Boss Rush (three seconds standing still under a boss's eye); this makes it pay off for the friend, so they are not one blow from falling again the moment they rise. It is only offered in a party, where it can matter.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'kindred-ember', name: 'Kindred Ember', rarity: 'common', party: true,
  text: 'Revive a friend: they rise with {heal} more health.',
  perk: { when: 'revive', then: 'reviveHeal' },
  levels: [{ heal: 0.1 }, { heal: 0.15 }, { heal: 0.2 }, { heal: 0.25 }] },
```

Numbers: a revived player rises with a third of their bar (40 of 120). Level I adds 10% of their bar (about 12, so 52), level IV 25% (about 30, so 70): from "one blow from falling" to "two blows". Revives come 0-3 a fight in a party, so its worth swings with the party's luck; a player alone never sees it.

## Engine work

- New top-level field `party: true`: the offer leaves it out of a run with one player (bots not counted, as revives are people only); validate.js: `party` is only `true`. Like `crate: true`, it is a filter on the offer, not on the kit.
- New `when: 'revive'`: fired for the reviver when a revive they ran finishes (server/simulation.js `reviveStep`, the `risen` entry's `by`). Perks only.
- New `then: 'reviveHeal'`: the risen player's health is `CONFIG.revive.health` plus the reviver's `heal`, of the risen player's bar (capped at the bar). `ABILITY_PERKS['revive/reviveHeal'] = ['heal']`. `heal` is already in `ABILITY_SHARES`.
- Emits `abilityPerk` `{ perk: 'revive/reviveHeal', body: reviver, target: risen }` for the drawing.
- Shared by the effect commons: the validate.js kind rule and the camera-feel.js common skip (see Spark Step).

## Multiplayer

The server decides the revive and already sends the risen player their health (`reviveHealth`, then the risen message's `hp`, which their browser applies). It adds `maxHpOf(risen) × heal` from the reviver's kit to that number. This is the one common that touches a teammate, and only for good: more health on rising. It never slows, moves, links or takes over them. Everyone sees the ring.

## Effect

Layered, timed from the rise (t = 0, the revive's existing rise burst in js/revive.js):

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00-0.20 | Flare | The revive's ember flares larger: the existing ember sprite scaled 1.6× and warmed, a bone rim on its edge | the ember's own colour, `#cfc8b6` rim |
| 0.05-0.50 | Ring | A flat ring of bone-white ash sweeps out along the ground from the ember to 3 m, hard leading edge, ragged ash trailing edge | `#f4f1e8` leading edge, `#cfc8b6` body, `#4a4740` ash, `#16130f` ink edge |
| 0.10-0.50 | Ash | 16 flat ash flakes lifted by the ring, drifting up and fading | `#cfc8b6`, `#8c877b` |

Budget (Common class): 1 pooled mesh (the ring; the flare is the revive's own ember sprite), 16 particles (9 on Normal), no light, no ribbon, no impact frame. Peak 0.2 s at the flare, all gone by 0.5 s. Reduced motion: no change needed (no flash; the flare is a scale step, once).

## Sound

Reuse `abilityHeal` (a soft rising chord) at pitch 1.1 and vel 0.55, played with the revive's own rise sound, for both the reviver and the risen.

## Camera

No camera kick: commons never take one. camera-feel.js's `perkFov` skips this common's `abilityPerk`.

## Images

# Glint

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Id | `glint` |

| Kind | Triggered perk (no key) |
| Trigger | `ready` (new): one of the holder's ability keys becomes full |
| Origin | New |

## Card

**A key fills: your next hit does {damage} more.** (9 words, 39 chars; level I reads "A key fills: your next hit does 40% more.")

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): an upright sword with a sharp four-point star sitting at its tip, a small square key cap beside the hilt.
- Hover loop (1.6 s): a key cap fills (0.4 s), a star glint slides down the blade and sits at its tip (0.3 s), the blade cuts and the star bursts (0.2 s); hold, fade.

## Idea

Each time an ability key fills, the blade glints and your next hit is heavier: a cue and a reward in one. A full key is easy to miss in a busy fight; the glint on the blade tells you without looking at the HUD, and the heavier next hit rewards answering at once (a heavy or a counter makes the most of it).

## Data

```js
{ id: 'glint', name: 'Glint', rarity: 'common',
  text: 'A key fills: your next hit does {damage} more.',
  perk: { when: 'ready', then: 'empower' },
  levels: [{ damage: 0.4 }, { damage: 0.55 }, { damage: 0.7 }, { damage: 0.85 }] },
```

Numbers: keys fill about 3-6 times a fight with one or two key abilities held. The next hit is 16 (a light) to about 61 (a full heavy) or 40-90 (a counter); level I adds 6-36 to it, so about 20-140 a fight, level IV about 40-300: in line with the other effect commons. It does nothing for a kit with no key ability. A second fill before the hit does not stack.

## Engine work

- New `when: 'ready'`: fired in `abilityGain` when a held key's charge reaches its ability's `charge` from below (once per fill; a key that stays full does not fire again).
- Reuses `then: 'empower'` (Vengeance's and Patience's: the next landed blow does `damage` more). New pair `ABILITY_PERKS['ready/empower'] = ['damage']`. Perk clocks: `glint` (0 or 1); `abilityStrike` spends it on the next landed blow like `hurt/empower`, with no time limit; cleared at the fight's end.
- Emits `abilityPerk` `{ perk: 'ready/empower' }` on the fill (the glint on the blade); the hit already emits `{ perk: 'empower' }`, whose cue (ability-fx.js) takes the colour of the rarity of the ability that empowered it (`picked[rarity]`), bone here.
- Shared by the effect commons: the validate.js kind rule and the camera-feel.js common skip (see Spark Step).

## Multiplayer

The key charge is counted in the holder's browser and on the server; `abilityStrike` runs where the enemies are owned. So the server detects the fill from its own count and spends the empower on the next blow it sees; the browser detects the fill from its count for the glint only. The two counts can differ by a point (a refused claim), so the glint can lead the server by a blow at worst: the damage is always the server's. It touches no teammate.

## Effect

Layered, timed from the key filling (t = 0); the spend at the empowered hit (t' = 0):

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00-0.25 | Slide | A sharp four-point star glint (0.3 m, hard thin points, a white core) slides from the hilt down the blade | `#f4f1e8` core, `#cfc8b6` points, `#16130f` hairline edge |
| 0.25 on | Sit | It sits at the blade's tip, turning slowly (no brightness flicker), until the next hit | as above |
| t' 0.00-0.20 | Burst | The star bursts on the struck enemy: 8 short bone-white streaks | `#f4f1e8` heads, `#8c877b` tails |

Budget (Common class): 1 pooled mesh (the star sprite), 8 particles (4 on Normal), no light, no ribbon, no impact frame. Peak 0.25 s at the slide, 0.2 s at the burst. Reduced motion: the star sits still instead of turning.

## Sound

`abilityGlint` (new, in `js/data/audio.js`): a bright ting (sine 2.8 kHz with a partial at 1.5×, 5 ms attack, decaying over 0.25 s), no other layer, vel 0.4, the holder's only. The empowered hit reuses `abilityEmpower` (a low thump under a hard ring) at pitch 1.15 and vel 0.55.

# Hunter's Pace

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Id | `hunters-pace` |
| Rarity | Common (bone ink `#cfc8b6`), 4 levels |
| Kind | Triggered perk (no key) |
| Trigger | `fightStart` (new): a fight begins (the moment the player gets control after the boss's entrance) |
| Origin | New |

## Card

**Fight start: free dashes for {time}.** (6 words, 31 chars; level I reads "Fight start: free dashes for 4 s.")

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): three chevrons in a row pointing right, with three short speed lines behind them.
- Hover loop (1.8 s): three dash bars glow (0.2 s), a figure dashes three times in quick succession with speed lines behind it (0.9 s), the bars dim back (0.2 s); hold, fade.

## Idea

The first seconds of every fight, dashes cost nothing: open with a rush. The start of a boss fight is the one moment you know exactly what comes next, and this turns it into a charge in: close the gap, circle to the flank, set up the first counter. It never helps later in the fight, so it changes how you open, not how you survive.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'hunters-pace', name: "Hunter's Pace", rarity: 'common',
  text: 'Fight start: free dashes for {time}.',
  perk: { when: 'fightStart', then: 'freeDash' },
  levels: [{ time: 4 }, { time: 5 }, { time: 6 }, { time: 7 }] },
```

Numbers: a dash is 0.36 s, so 4 s holds up to 11 dashes, in practice 4-6 used, against the 3 charges a player starts with; level IV's 7 s covers the opening exchange of most bosses. It deals no damage: its worth is the safe, fast approach and a first counter set up sooner.

## Engine work

- New `when: 'fightStart'`: fired on the holder's body when a fight begins (Boss Rush: control given after the boss's entrance; js/game.js's fight start, the same moment the fight's timer starts). Perks only.
- Reuses Last Breath's `then: 'freeDash'`. New pair `ABILITY_PERKS['fightStart/freeDash'] = ['time']`. Perk clocks: `hunt` (s left), set to `time` on the trigger, counted down in `abilityClocks`. `Player.freeDash()` also returns true while `hunt` > 0. Emits `abilityPerk` `{ perk: 'fightStart/freeDash' }`.
- Shared by the effect commons: the validate.js kind rule and the camera-feel.js common skip (see Spark Step).

## Multiplayer

A perk on the holder's own body: their browser runs it from the fight's start it already receives from the server (each client owns its movement and dashes). The server needs nothing. It moves only its holder. The speed lines are drawn in the holder's browser, as every perk cue is today.

## Effect

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00 to time | Bars (HUD) | The dash charge bars glow white with a thin bone rim and stay full, dimming in the last 1 s to show the end | `#f4f1e8` fill, `#cfc8b6` rim |
| t' 0.00-0.30 | Lines | 10 bone-white radial speed lines streak back off the body along the dash (flat hard streaks, 0.6-1.2 m) | `#f4f1e8` heads, `#cfc8b6` body, `#16130f` tail tips |
| t' 0.20-0.40 | Fade | The lines thin and fade | to transparent |

## Sound

```js
{ id: 'mirror-shard', name: 'Mirror Shard', rarity: 'common',
  text: 'Deflect a shot: it flies back.',
  power: { when: 'parryShot', then: 'reflect' },
  levels: [{ damage: 30 }, { damage: 40 }, { damage: 50 }, { damage: 60 }] },
```

Numbers: 30 is about three quarters of a counter, for the harder timing on a small fast shape. Against a boss that shoots, 3-6 deflected shots a fight is about 90-180 at level I and 180-360 at level IV. Eight of the eighteen boss files in js/data/bosses have an attack with `projectile`; against the rest it does nothing, so its average is below the other effect commons, by design: a specialist pick. No cooldown: shots are few.

## Engine work

- New `when: 'parryShot'`: today no bolt can be deflected (js/projectiles.js: "it can never be parried"; `canParryHit` refuses `bolt`). For a holder of a `parryShot` power only, a bolt reaching the player with a deflect press armed (`CONFIG.parry.arm`, the same window as a blow, widened by Keen Eye) and the player facing it is deflected instead of hitting: it takes no health and no block cost. `ctx`: `{ enemy: the shooter, bolt }`. Without the power, bolts behave as now. A deflected shot is not a `parry`: it opens no counter, gives no key charge and fires no `parry` power.
- New `then: 'reflect'`: the bolt turns round and flies straight back at the shooter's chest at its own speed (no arc); on reaching the shooter's body, `damage` to it as a power's blow. If the shooter is dead or out of the bolt's life, it flies on and expires. It passes through every other body and stops on walls as bolts do. `ABILITY_POWERS['parryShot/reflect'] = ['damage']`.
- `validate.js`: `parryShot/reflect` needs `damage` (the existing plan check).
- Shared by the effect commons: the validate.js kind rule and the camera-feel.js common skip (see Spark Step).

## Multiplayer

Each browser flies the server's shots against its own player, so the deflect is seen only by the holder's browser: `parryShot` joins `ABILITY_CLAIMS`. The claim names the shooter and the shot; the server checks it fired that shot at this player within the bolt's life, the shooter is alive, and the player's pose was facing it, then resolves the damage when the bolt's return time (distance / speed) has passed. It hits the shooter only; a teammate in the way sees the bolt pass through them. Everyone sees the returning bolt (drawn from the server's `abilityPower` event, from the holder to the shooter).

## Effect

Layered, timed from the deflect (t = 0); the return reaches the shooter at t = R (distance / speed):

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00 | Clash | A small hard four-point star where the bolt meets the blade (0.4 m) | `#f4f1e8` core, `#cfc8b6` points |
| 0.00 | Turn | The bolt's own mesh snaps to bone white with a dark ink outline (tinted, the projectile pool's bolt) | `#f4f1e8` body, `#cfc8b6` head, `#16130f` outline |
| 0.00 to R | Trail | A thin strip behind it scattered with flat mirror-shard triangles (hard edges, one bright face, one dark), 14 shards shed along the path and turning as they fall | `#f4f1e8` bright face, `#8c877b` dark face, `#16130f` edges |
| R | Hit | A second small star on the shooter's chest | as the clash |
| R to R + 0.3 | Fade | Shards and star fade | to transparent |

Budget (Common class): 2 pooled meshes (the star sprite, the trail strip; the bolt is the projectile pool's own), 14 particles (8 on Normal), no light, no ribbon, no impact frame. Peak 0.1 s at the clash; the return lasts as long as the flight (under 0.6 s at bolt speeds and boss ranges). Reduced motion: no change needed (no flash).

## Sound

`abilityMirror` (new, in `js/data/audio.js`): a glassy transient clink (sine 3.5 kHz with high-passed noise at 6 kHz, 12 ms), a body of a pitched whoosh of the returning bolt (band-passed noise sweeping 2 kHz to 1 kHz over 0.3 s), no tail. The hit on the shooter reuses the projectile's own hit sound.

## Camera

No camera kick: commons never take one.

## Images

- `img/mirror-shard-1.webp`: the swordsman deflecting an incoming fiery projectile, the projectile turning white and flying back toward the boss with a trail of mirror shards.

# Shatter Guard

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Id | `shatter-guard` |
| Rarity | Common (bone ink `#cfc8b6`), 4 levels |
| Kind | Triggered power (no key) |
| Trigger | `crack` (new): a counter of the holder's cracks an enemy's guard (a crack, not the Finishing Blow itself) |
| Origin | New |

## Card

**Crack a guard: its shards cut the boss.** (8 words, 39 chars)

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): a curved guard plate with a jagged crack through it and three small triangular shards curving back toward it.
- Hover loop (1.6 s): a cut lands on a plate (0.2 s), a crack runs across it (0.2 s), three shards burst off and curve back into it (0.4 s); hold, fade.

## Idea

Each counter that cracks the boss's guard throws shards of that guard back into it. The cracks are the road to the Finishing Blow, but today they are a tint and a count; this makes them physical, a guard you can see breaking, and pays each one a little on the way.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'shatter-guard', name: 'Shatter Guard', rarity: 'common',
  text: 'Crack a guard: its shards cut the boss.',
  power: { when: 'crack', then: 'shards' },
  levels: [{ damage: 22 }, { damage: 28 }, { damage: 34 }, { damage: 40 }] },
```

Numbers: two cracks come before each Finishing Blow, so of 4-8 counters a fight about 3-5 are cracks: about 65-110 more at level I and 120-200 at level IV, in line with the other effect commons. No cooldown: counters space it.

## Engine work

- New `when: 'crack'`: fired when the holder's counter adds a crack to an enemy's guard (the `guardCrack` event with `by` the holder and `cracks` rising, from `crackGuard`); not when the cracks fade or a Finishing Blow spends them. `ctx`: `{ enemy }`.
- New `then: 'shards'`: `damage` to that enemy as a power's blow, 0.12 s after the crack so the shards are seen to land (a `running` entry with one strike, as Echo Step's). Add it to `ON_ENEMY`. `ABILITY_POWERS['crack/shards'] = ['damage']`.
- A power's blow is never a counter, so the shards never add a crack of their own.
- Shared by the effect commons: the validate.js kind rule and the camera-feel.js common skip (see Spark Step).

## Multiplayer

The server counts the cracks and grants the Finishing Blow (`Simulation.hit`), so it sees each crack itself: no claim. It triggers `crack` for the striker whose counter cracked it. It hits that enemy only. Everyone sees the shards.

## Effect

Layered, timed from the crack (t = 0):

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00 | Mark | A short jagged crack decal on the enemy's body where the counter landed (one sprite), hard dark lines with a white inner edge | `#16130f` lines, `#f4f1e8` inner edge |
| 0.00-0.12 | Burst | 12 glassy shards (flat triangles, one bright face, one shaded, hard edges) burst out of the mark 0.6-1 m | `#f4f1e8` bright face, `#cfc8b6` edge, `#8c877b` shade |
| 0.12-0.30 | Return | They curve back and drive into the body at the mark, vanishing as they enter | as above |
| 0.20-0.45 | Fade | The mark fades | to transparent |

Budget (Common class): 1 pooled mesh (the crack sprite), 12 particles (7 on Normal), no light, no ribbon, no impact frame. Peak 0.12 s at the burst. Reduced motion: no change needed (no flash).

## Sound

`abilityShatter` (new, in `js/data/audio.js`): a glass-break transient (noise band-passed at 3-8 kHz, 30 ms), a body of tinkling shards (6 sine blips at random pitches in 2-4 kHz over 0.25 s), a short tail (verb 0.35). Under the counter's own hit sound, vel 0.5.

## Camera

No camera kick: commons never take one (the counter already has its own).

## Images

- `img/shatter-guard-1.webp`: a counter slash cracking the guard of an armoured boss, glassy white shards bursting off the crack and curving back into it.
