# Ember Mail

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Id | `ember-mail` |
| Rarity | Rare (cool blue `#8fb8dc`), 3 levels |
| Kind | Key 2, Guard |
| Trigger | `press`: key 2 pressed with its charge full (15, 14, 13 points) |
| Origin | New |

## Card

**Ember armour takes {hits} blows for you.** (7 words, 35 chars)

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): three overlapping curved plates over a shoulder line, the top one cracked with a small chip flying off.
- Hover loop (1.8 s): the key 2 square lights (0.2 s); glowing plates fly in and lock onto a small figure (0.3 s); a boss blow lands and one layer of plates shatters off while the figure doesn't flinch (0.5 s); a second blow takes the next layer (0.5 s); fade.

## Idea

Spectral plates of blue-hot embers lock onto you and take the next blows whole, cracking off one layer at a time. It is the plainest guard: no timing at all, just a buffer for the moment you know you will be caught, and every blow it takes shows on your body as a shattering plate.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'ember-mail', name: 'Ember Mail', rarity: 'rare', key: 'guard',
  text: 'Ember armour takes {hits} blows for you.',
  perk: { when: 'press', then: 'armour' },
  levels: [
    { charge: 15, hits: 1, time: 8 },
    { charge: 14, hits: 2, time: 8 },
    { charge: 13, hits: 2, time: 10 },
  ] },
```

Numbers: one blow taken whole is worth about 34 health (the median boss blow on a 120 bar) and up to 70 on a big one, close to Mending's 24-36 at about the same charge. Level II's second blow doubles it; level III keeps two and holds 10 s so the armour is rarely wasted. 15 points at 1-1.4 a second is armour every 11-15 s; 8-10 s means it is usually spent before the next press, so it never stacks.

## Engine work

- New perk `press/armour` in `ABILITY_PERKS` (`['charge', 'hits', 'time']`), with `plates` (blows left) and `mail` (s left) in `abilityPerkState`; `abilityClocks` counts `mail` down and clears `plates` at 0. A new press sets both afresh (no stacking).
- `Player.takeHit`: while `perk.plates > 0`, a landing blow does nothing to the body (no damage, knock or flinch; a counter window stays open), and `perk.plates` drops by one with an `abilityPerk` `perk: 'press/armour'` and `left`. Any blow counts (deflectable or not, area hits and shots included) except a grab (`seize`, `pull`), which breaks every plate at once and takes the holder as usual. A fall, a burn over time and a `destined` drain are not blows.
- `validate.js`: `press/armour` needs `charge`, `hits` (a whole number), `time`.

## Multiplayer

The armour is its holder's own defence: the browser takes the blow on its plates (the client owns its health) and tells the server it took no damage as it already does. The server knows the press and the level, so it accepts at most `hits` blows taken whole within `time` s. Holder only; the plates never cover a teammate.

## Effect

Layered, timed from the press (t = 0) and from each blow taken (t = h):

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00-0.25 | Lock | Flat curved plates (two pauldrons, a breastplate, two vambraces) fly in from 1 m out and lock onto the body with a hard snap; each plate is 2-tone, a white-hot seam down its middle, blue edges, ink outline | `#2c5f8a` plate, `#8fb8dc` edge, `#f2f6fa` seam, `#0b0d12` outline |
| 0.25-`time` | Hold | Plates glow steadily; 8 ember flakes rise off them each second; level II-III show two layers, the outer one larger | `#8fb8dc` flakes |
| h | Crack | The outer layer cracks white in one frame | `#f2f6fa` |
| h+0.02-h+0.40 | Shatter | Its plates burst outward into 12 flat shards and 10 embers, flung away from the blow | `#8fb8dc` shards, `#f2f6fa` embers |
| last 1.0 s | Dim | Unspent plates dim and flicker slowly (1 Hz) so their end is readable | `#2c5f8a` |
| `time`-+0.3 | Fall | Unspent plates loosen and fall to ash | to transparent |

Budget (Rare class): 5 pooled meshes (a plate set drawn as one mesh per layer, two layers; a shard sheet; a crack sheet; a flake emitter) + 22 particles a shatter and 8 flakes a second (at most 40 alive; 22 on Normal), 1 effect light (blue, 0.2 s a shatter, intensity × 0.65 on Normal), no ribbon, no impact frame. Peak 0.4 s a shatter. Reduced motion: the last-second flicker becomes a steady dim.

## Sound

`abilityMail` (new, in `js/data/audio.js`): on the press three quick metal locks (white noise band-passed at 3.5 kHz, 10 ms each, 60 ms apart) over a body of a low ember roar (brown noise low-passed at 400 Hz, 0.5 s); on each shatter a transient clang (sine 520 Hz with a 2.76 partial, 2 ms attack, 0.3 s), a crackle of embers (white noise high-passed at 4 kHz, short grains, 0.3 s), a tail of falling metal (band-passed noise at 1.5 kHz, 0.4 s).

## Camera

No new entry: js/camera-feel.js treats a blow taken by the plates as a blocked one (the hurt push × `blockMul`), and the perk kick plays on the press.

## Images

- `img/ember-mail-1.webp`: spectral armour plates of glowing blue embers locking onto the swordsman, one plate shattering off as a boss blow lands.

# Iron Root

| Trigger | `press`: key 2 pressed with its charge full (13, 12, 11 points) |

## Card

**For {time}, nothing staggers you; take {cut} less.** (8 words, 41 chars)

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): two feet planted on a floor line, three branching root lines spreading down and out from them.
- Hover loop (1.8 s): the key 2 square lights (0.2 s); dark roots crack out across the floor from a small figure's feet (0.3 s); the figure keeps swinging while two boss blows land on it without a flinch, each with a small number (1.0 s); the roots withdraw; fade.

## Idea

Iron roots grow from your feet into the floor and your body takes a steel sheen: for a few seconds you trade blows with the boss without flinching and take less from each. It is the aggressive guard, for the player who would rather finish their string than dodge out of it, and it pairs with heavies, whose long swings are what a flinch usually costs.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'iron-root', name: 'Iron Root', rarity: 'rare', key: 'guard',
  text: 'For {time}, nothing staggers you; take {cut} less.',
  perk: { when: 'press', then: 'root' },
  levels: [
    { charge: 13, time: 4, cut: 0.3 },
    { charge: 12, time: 4.5, cut: 0.35 },
    { charge: 11, time: 5, cut: 0.4 },
  ] },
```

Numbers: in 4-5 s a boss lands one to three blows on a player who stands and trades; 30-40% off each is about 10-14 health a median blow, 20-40 health a press. The bigger value is not flinching: a heavy string (up to 56 a blow) finishes instead of being cut off, about one or two extra heavies' worth of damage. 13 points at 1-1.4 a second is a press every 9-13 s, cheaper than the guards that take a whole blow.

## Engine work

- New perk `press/root` in `ABILITY_PERKS` (`['charge', 'time', 'cut']`), with `root` (s left) and `rootV` in `abilityPerkState`; `abilityClocks` counts it down.
- `Player.takeHit`: while `perk.root > 0`, damage is × (1 - `cut`) (after the block's cut, if blocking), knock is 0, and neither `PS.HURT` nor `PS.STAGGER` is set: the body keeps whatever it was doing, a drink included. Grabs (`seize`, `pull`) still take the holder: they are the boss's answer to someone standing still.
- `cut` is a share of the blow: add it to `ABILITY_SHARES` (at most 1) so `validate.js` holds it below 1, and the card shows it as a percentage.
- `validate.js`: `press/root` needs `charge`, `time`, `cut`.

## Multiplayer

The roots are their holder's own defence (the client owns its health and its flinch). The server needs nothing new beyond accepting the press: the client reports its own health as it already does. Holder only; the roots are drawn on the floor but have no collision and never slow a teammate who walks over them.

Layered, timed from the press (t = 0):

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00-0.30 | Grow | Flat dark iron roots crack out across the floor from the feet, 2.4 m across, hard-edged and branching, each with a thin glowing vein down its middle; a few stone chips kick up | `#2a2827` roots, `#8fb8dc` veins, `#0b0d12` ink edges |
| 0.00-0.20 | Sheen | A steel sheen sweeps up the body from the feet: a flat bright band of rim light | `#cfe4f2` |
| 0.30-`time` | Hold | The roots stay round the feet; when the holder moves more than 1 m the old roots sink and new ones crack out under them (0.2 s). Each blow taken sends a pulse of blue down the veins into the floor | `#8fb8dc` pulse |
| each blow | Bite | 6 grey stone chips jump from the floor and the body doesn't move; a short hard white spark at the contact | `#9a958c`, `#f2f6fa` |
| last 0.6 s | Wane | The veins dim from the tips inward | to `#2c5f8a` |
| `time`-+0.3 | Withdraw | The roots pull back into the feet and the sheen fades | to transparent |

# Vanishing Step

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Id | `vanishing-step` |
| Rarity | Rare (cool blue `#8fb8dc`), 3 levels |
| Kind | Key 2, Guard |
| Trigger | `press`: key 2 pressed with its charge full (12, 11, 10 points) |
| Origin | New |

## Card

**Refill all dashes; vanish for {time}.** (6 words, 32 chars)

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): a figure's outline breaking into five small petal shapes on one side, three short bars beneath it.
- Hover loop (1.4 s): the key 2 square lights (0.2 s); a small figure with empty dash bars is caught in a boss's wind-up; it bursts into a swirl of blue petals (0.3 s) and the blow passes through empty air (0.3 s); the figure reforms beside it and the three dash bars flash full (0.4 s); fade.

## Idea

The instant escape. You blink out in a swirl of blue petals, untouchable and unseen for a moment, and every dash comes back. It is the guard for the moment a newcomer has spent all their dashes in panic and the boss's next blow is already falling, and for a skilled player it is three more perfect dodges in the bank.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'vanishing-step', name: 'Vanishing Step', rarity: 'rare', key: 'guard',
  text: 'Refill all dashes; vanish for {time}.',
  perk: { when: 'press', then: 'vanish' },
  levels: [
    { charge: 12, time: 0.6 },
    { charge: 11, time: 0.7 },
    { charge: 10, time: 0.8 },
  ] },
```

Numbers: three dashes refill one at a time over 1.3 s each, so a full refill from empty is about 3.9 s of waiting given back at once, plus 0.6-0.8 s untouchable (two dashes' i-frames, 0.3 s each). It avoids no more than one blow by itself, so it is the cheapest guard: 12-10 points at 1-1.4 a second, a press every 7-12 s.

## Engine work

- New perk `press/vanish` in `ABILITY_PERKS` (`['charge', 'time']`), with `vanish` (s left) in `abilityPerkState`; `abilityClocks` counts it down.
- On the press: every dash charge is set full; for `time` s the body is untouchable (`invulnerable()` also checks `perk.vanish > 0`) and drawn hidden. The holder can move, dash and block while vanished; an attack or a flask ends the vanish at once.
- A blow that meets the holder while vanished passes through without a perfect dodge: no counter window, no dodge points (so it can't farm counters or charge).
- Targeting: while vanished the holder can't be chosen as a target (an enemy keeps its current swing but does not turn to track them; the server's aggro skips them for new choices).
- `validate.js`: `press/vanish` needs `charge`, `time`.

## Multiplayer

The vanish is its holder's own defence and movement (the client owns both); the server accepts the press, then knows the holder is untouchable and not a target for `time` s plus its slack. To teammates the holder is drawn as the petal swirl and a faint 15% outline, so a friend never loses track of where they are. It never moves or hides a teammate.

## Effect

Layered, timed from the press (t = 0):

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00-0.08 | Break | The body breaks from the edges inward into 36 flat petals (hard-edged, two-tone, ink outline); the body is hidden at 0.08 s | `#8fb8dc` petal, `#f2f6fa` inner tone, `#0b0d12` outline |
| 0.08-`time` | Swirl | The petals swirl in a tight column round where the body is (following it as it moves), turning and fluttering | as above |
| 0.00-0.30 | Bars | The three dash bars on the HUD flash full, left to right, 50 ms apart | `#f2f6fa` |
| `time`-+0.15 | Reform | The petals pull in and the body reforms from the middle out | as above |
| +0.15-+0.6 | Settle | 8 petals drift down and fade on the floor | to transparent |

Budget (Rare class): 1 pooled mesh (the petal swirl as one instanced mesh) + 36 petals (20 on Normal), 1 effect light (blue, low, while vanished, intensity × 0.65 on Normal), no ribbon, no impact frame. Peak 0.08 s. Reduced motion: the petals swirl at half speed.

## Sound

`abilityVanish` (new, in `js/data/audio.js`): a transient of a soft air pop (white noise high-passed at 3 kHz, 20 ms), a body of a swirl of petals (pink noise band-passed sweeping 800 Hz to 3 kHz and back over `time`, low gain), a tail on the reform (a rising glass note, sine 988 Hz, 0.4 s). The dash bars filling each tick (the normal dash refill chime, three times, 50 ms apart).

## Camera

No new entry: the perk kick plays on the press; the view never moves on its own while the body is hidden.

## Images

- `img/vanishing-step-1.webp`: the swordsman dissolving into a swirl of blue petals as a boss attack passes through empty air.

# Still Water

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Id | `still-water` |
| Rarity | Rare (cool blue `#8fb8dc`), 3 levels |
| Kind | Key 2, Guard |
| Trigger | `press`: key 2 pressed with its charge full (16, 15, 14 points) |
| Origin | New |

## Card

**A pool heals {heal} over {time}.** (6 words, 22 chars)

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): a flat ellipse on a floor line with two inner rings and a small droplet falling into its centre.
- Hover loop (1.8 s): the key 2 square lights (0.2 s); a mirror-still pool spreads from a small figure's feet (0.3 s); slow rings cross it while the figure's bar climbs steadily (1.0 s); a second figure steps in at the edge and its bar climbs a little; fade.

## Idea

A pool of still water spreads on the floor; standing in it heals you over a few seconds, and a friend who steps in heals a little too. It is the slow, generous heal: more than Mending in total, but it asks you to hold your ground in one place while the boss is still swinging, so it rewards pressing it in a boss's quiet moment.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'still-water', name: 'Still Water', rarity: 'rare', key: 'guard',
  text: 'A pool heals {heal} over {time}.',
  perk: { when: 'press', then: 'pool' },
  levels: [
    { charge: 16, time: 5, heal: 0.25, radius: 2.5 },
    { charge: 15, time: 5, heal: 0.3, radius: 2.7 },
    { charge: 14, time: 5, heal: 0.35, radius: 2.9 },
  ] },
```

Numbers: 25-35% of the bar over 5 s is 30-42 health, a little more than Mending's 24-36 at a slightly higher charge, but only for the time spent inside a 2.5-2.9 m circle. 16 points at 1-1.4 a second is a pool every 12-16 s. A teammate inside heals at a third of the rate (`CONFIG.abilities.shared.pool` 0.33): at most 8-12% of their own bar over the 5 s.

## Engine work

- New perk `press/pool` in `ABILITY_PERKS` (`['charge', 'time', 'heal', 'radius']`). Though a perk, it is placed in the world: on the press the pool is fixed at the holder's feet for `time` s (it does not follow them).
- A shared list of live pools (`{ holder, x, y, z, radius, rate, until }`, a fixed pool of 4, one a player). Each step, a body standing inside one (within `radius` m and its floor's height) heals `heal / time` of its bar per s (its holder) or `× CONFIG.abilities.shared.pool` of that (anyone else). Stepping out pauses the heal; the time runs on. Two pools on one body never add: the best one counts.
- `CONFIG.abilities.shared: { pool: 0.33 }`.
- `validate.js`: `press/pool` needs `charge`, `time`, `heal` (a share, at most 1), `radius`; `shared.pool` from 0 to 1.

## Multiplayer

The press is claimed like every press, and the server tells every browser the pool's place, `radius`, rate and `time` (`abilityPerk` `perk: 'press/pool'`, the shared guard perk). Each browser heals its own body while it stands inside (each client owns its health), and the server checks that heal against the pools it knows. The shared benefit, its size stated: a teammate inside heals one third of the holder's rate, 8-12% of their bar over 5 s at most, and nothing else. The pool has no collision and never slows, pushes or moves anyone.

## Effect

Layered, timed from the press (t = 0):

pool.md:
# Hourglass

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Id | `hourglass` |
| Rarity | Rare (cool blue `#8fb8dc`), 3 levels |
| Kind | Key 2, Guard |
| Trigger | `press`: key 2 pressed with its charge full (18, 17, 16 points) |
| Origin | New |

## Card

**Rewind place and health to {time} ago.** (7 words, 33 chars)

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): a curved path line ending in a small figure, an arrow running back along it, three short tick marks across the path like a clock's.
- Hover loop (1.8 s): a small figure runs a curve and takes a blow, its bar dropping (0.6 s); the key 2 square lights (0.2 s); the figure snaps back along its path through a line of blue afterimages, tick marks clicking past (0.4 s), and its bar refills to where it was (0.2 s); fade.

## Idea

Time unwinds for you alone. You snap back along your own path to where you stood a few seconds ago, with the health you had then. It is the undo button for a mistake you have already made, the only guard you press after the blow lands, and the most expensive one, because it can erase a whole bad exchange.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'hourglass', name: 'Hourglass', rarity: 'rare', key: 'guard',
  text: 'Rewind place and health to {time} ago.',
  perk: { when: 'press', then: 'rewind' },
  levels: [
    { charge: 18, time: 3 },
    { charge: 17, time: 3.5 },
    { charge: 16, time: 4 },
  ] },
```

Numbers: in 3-4 s a careless player takes one or two blows, so a rewind gives back 34-70 health on a median boss (28-58% of the bar), more than Mending's 20-30% but only after a bad exchange; after a clean one it gives nothing but the reposition. 18 points at 1-1.4 a second is a rewind every 13-18 s, the slowest guard to fill. Rewinding never lowers health: the holder keeps the higher of now and then, so a rewind after a heal costs nothing.

## Engine work

- New perk `press/rewind` in `ABILITY_PERKS` (`['charge', 'time']`).
- The holder's body records its trail: a fixed ring buffer of `{ x, y, z, yaw, hp }` every 0.1 s, `CONFIG.abilities.rewind.slots` (41) entries made at load, enough for 4 s. Nothing is allocated per step.
- On the press: the body slides back along the recorded trail to the entry `time` s old over `CONFIG.abilities.rewind.glide` (0.35 s), untouchable while it slides (as a dash's i-frames) and not steering; then its health is the higher of now and the entry's. Dash charges, the flasks and the other keys' charge are not rewound.
- It can't be pressed in a grip (`PS.HELD`), during a Finishing Blow, or while dead. A trail entry over a pit or off the floor's edge is skipped for the nearest earlier safe one.
- `validate.js`: `press/rewind` needs `charge`, `time`; `CONFIG.abilities.rewind` `slots` a whole number covering the longest `time` at 0.1 s, `glide` above 0.

## Multiplayer

The rewind is its holder's own movement and health (the client owns both). The server range-checks it: the place rewound to must be within its slack of a pose it saw from that holder `time` s ago, and the health restored at most the highest health it accepted from them in that window. The server's targeting sees the holder at their new place. Holder only: it never moves, rewinds or touches a teammate.

## Effect

Layered, timed from the press (t = 0):

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00-0.05 | Catch | A flat ribbon traces the recorded path on the floor in one stroke, ink-edged, with a tick mark across it every 0.5 s of path | `#8fb8dc` ribbon, `#f2f6fa` ticks, `#0b0d12` ink |
| 0.05-0.40 | Rewind | The body slides back along it; 5 afterimages, flat-shaded copies of the holder in the poses they held, appear along the path in reverse order and fade one by one as it passes them | `#8fb8dc` at 50%, `#f2f6fa` rim |
| 0.05-0.40 | Hands | A thin clock hand sweeps backwards once round a faint dial on the floor at the start point | `#f2f6fa` |
| 0.40 | Arrive | A hard ring on the floor at the arrival point; the health bar refills with a blue sweep from its right end | `#8fb8dc` |
| 0.40-0.90 | Fade | The ribbon fades from the start point to the arrival point | to transparent |

Budget (Rare class): the ribbon (1) + 5 afterimages (pooled copies of the player figure, drawn flat, one set a player) + 2 pooled meshes (dial, arrival ring) + 12 tick particles (7 on Normal), 1 effect light (blue, 0.4 s, intensity × 0.65 on Normal), no impact frame. Peak 0.4 s. Reduced motion: the afterimages appear together and fade, not in sequence.

## Sound

`abilityRewind` (new, in `js/data/audio.js`): a transient of a clock's tick played backwards (a short noise click with a reversed envelope, 30 ms), a body of the fight's sound drawn backwards (band-passed noise sweeping down from 3 kHz to 400 Hz over 0.35 s, with four soft ticks at 1.2 kHz along it), a tail of a low bell landing (sine 196 Hz with a 2.4 partial, 0.8 s).

## Camera

`CONFIG.camera.feel.powers.rewind = [-1, 0.03]`: a small pull in on arrival. The view follows the body as it slides (it is the holder's own movement), never cutting.

## Images

- `img/hourglass-1.webp`: the swordsman snapping backward along their recent path, a ribbon of blue afterimages running in reverse with clock-hand tick marks.

# Binding Seal

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Id | `binding-seal` |
| Rarity | Rare (cool blue `#8fb8dc`), 3 levels |
| Kind | Key 2, Guard |
| Trigger | `press`: key 2 pressed with its charge full (16, 15, 14 points) |
| Origin | New |

## Card

**Seal the boss's next attack.** (5 words, 28 chars)

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): a long narrow paper strip with three brush marks on it, its lower end curling into a small flame.
- Hover loop (1.8 s): the key 2 square lights (0.2 s); a strip of paper flies from a small figure and sticks to a boss (0.3 s); the boss winds up its blow in full (0.5 s); the strip burns away and the blow sputters out into smoke before it lands (0.5 s); fade.

## Idea

Slap a paper seal of light onto the boss. Its next attack shows its whole wind-up, then fizzles out at the moment it should land, and the boss stands there open. The tell is never hidden, so it teaches as it protects: the player sees the attack they would have had to answer, and gets the opening instead.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'binding-seal', name: 'Binding Seal', rarity: 'rare', key: 'guard',
  text: "Seal the boss's next attack.",
  power: { when: 'press', then: 'seal' },
  levels: [
    { charge: 16, time: 6 },
    { charge: 15, time: 7 },
    { charge: 14, time: 8 },
  ] },
```

Numbers: bosses start an attack every 1.6-5.6 s, so a seal of 6-8 s almost always catches one. One attack sealed is a whole combo not thrown (one to five blows, 34 each on a median boss) plus a recovery the party can punish. 16 points at 1-1.4 a second is a seal every 12-16 s, as dear as the dome, because it covers everyone the boss would have hit.

## Engine work

- New power `press/seal` in `ABILITY_POWERS` (`['charge', 'time']`), on the press target (`pressTarget`).
- The enemy gets `sealed` (s left) and its holder. The next attack it begins while sealed plays its wind-up as normal (the tell, sound and every warning shape), then at its first active frame no hitbox is made for any of its hits, no impact, shot or area mark is spawned, and the enemy plays the attack's recovery `CONFIG.abilities.seal.recover` (0.4 s) longer. `sealed` goes to 0. Emitted as `abilityPower` `then: 'seal'` with `sputter: true`.
- One seal on an enemy at a time: a press on a sealed enemy renews `sealed` to the new `time` (nothing stacks). A seal still on when its time runs out falls off unused.
- The sputter counts as nothing for the Finishing Blow or posture (it isn't a hit), and it never ends a phase change or a scripted move (a boss's arrival, a phase transition): those are not attacks.
- `validate.js`: `press/seal` needs `charge`, `time`; `CONFIG.abilities.seal.recover` 0 or more.

## Multiplayer

The server owns the boss, so it applies the seal from the accepted press and runs the sputter; every browser draws it from the `abilityPower` events. The seal is on the boss, not on any teammate: it stops the sealed attack whoever it was aimed at, which helps the party without moving, slowing or linking anyone. With several holders in a party, one seal a boss at a time keeps it from chaining.

## Effect

Layered, timed from the press (t = 0) and from the sealed attack's wind-up (t = w) and active frame (t = a):

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00-0.20 | Throw | A long paper strip, 0.25 × 1.4 m, flies from the holder's hand in a flat arc and slaps onto the boss's chest or back (whichever side faces the holder, never the weapon arm) | `#f2f6fa` paper, `#8fb8dc` edge, `#0b0d12` brush marks |
| 0.20-`time` | Hold | The strip clings and flutters; its three brush marks glow faintly | `#8fb8dc` marks |
| w-a | Burn | The strip burns away from its lower end over the wind-up: a hard white-blue flame front with ink-black curl behind it. The boss's wind-up is never covered: the strip stays on the torso and is under 1.5 m long | `#f2f6fa` flame, `#8fb8dc` edge, `#0b0d12` curl |
| a-a+0.5 | Sputter | At the weapon, where the blow would land, a puff of grey smoke and 10 ink flakes; the weapon's own trail is cut short | `#9a958c` smoke, `#0b0d12` flakes |
| a+0.5 | Open | A thin blue ring on the floor round the boss for its stretched recovery | `#8fb8dc` |

Budget (Rare class): 3 pooled meshes (strip, smoke sheet, floor ring) + 10 flakes and 8 burn embers (18 particles; 10 on Normal), 1 effect light (blue, 0.3 s at the sputter, intensity × 0.65 on Normal), no ribbon, no impact frame. Peak 0.5 s. The boss's undeflectable wind-up glows blue too (`rollOnlyGlow`), so the seal leads with white paper and keeps its blue to thin edges, off the weapon. Reduced motion: no change needed.

## Sound

`abilitySeal` (new, in `js/data/audio.js`): on the press a sharp paper slap (white noise band-passed at 2.5 kHz, 15 ms) and a short bright chime (sine 1318 Hz, 0.4 s); as the strip burns a quiet crackle (high-passed noise grains, the wind-up's length); on the sputter a transient of a fizzle (band-passed noise sweeping 3 kHz down to 300 Hz in 0.25 s), a body of a dull puff (brown noise, 0.2 s), and no hit sound.

## Camera

`CONFIG.camera.feel.powers.seal = [0.8, 0]`: a small widening on the sputter, so the open boss reads.

## Images

- `img/binding-seal-1.webp`: a long strip of glowing blue paper seal with brush marks stuck on a boss mid wind-up, burning away as the attack fizzles.

pool.md:
# Unbroken

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Id | `unbroken` |
| Rarity | Rare (cool blue `#8fb8dc`), 3 levels |
| Kind | Key 2, Guard |
| Trigger | `press`: key 2 pressed with its charge full (18, 17, 16 points) |
| Origin | New |

## Card

**For {time}, no blow can kill you.** (7 words, 28 chars)

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): a kneeling figure with its sword planted, a tall flame shape rising above its head.
- Hover loop (1.8 s): the key 2 square lights (0.2 s); a blue flame rises over a small figure with a near-empty bar (0.3 s); a huge blow lands, the figure drops to one knee with a sliver left and the flame flares tall (0.6 s); the figure stands and strikes back (0.4 s); fade.

## Idea

A blue flame of will. For a few seconds nothing takes you below a sliver of health: the all-in moment, when you are low and the boss is nearly down and you decide to stand and finish it. It never heals, so the moment it ends you are as fragile as before, and the choice of when to press it is the whole skill.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'unbroken', name: 'Unbroken', rarity: 'rare', key: 'guard',
  text: 'For {time}, no blow can kill you.',
  perk: { when: 'press', then: 'undying' },
  levels: [
    { charge: 18, time: 3 },
    { charge: 17, time: 4 },
    { charge: 16, time: 5 },
  ] },
```

Numbers: 3-5 s is one boss combo and the punish after it. On full health it does nothing, so its value is all at low health, where it is worth a whole life for a few seconds. 18 points at 1-1.4 a second is a press every 13-18 s, as dear as Hourglass. It never heals, so it never makes a player safe for longer than its time.

## Engine work

- New perk `press/undying` in `ABILITY_PERKS` (`['charge', 'time']`), with `undying` (s left) in `abilityPerkState`; `abilityClocks` counts it down.
- `Player.takeHit` and every other health loss (a burn, a `destined` drain, a hazard's damage): while `perk.undying > 0`, health never drops below `CONFIG.abilities.undying.floor` (1 health). A blow that would have killed plays as a stagger (`PS.STAGGER`, the kneel) and emits `abilityPerk` `perk: 'press/undying'` with `saved: true`.
- A fall into a pit still kills (it isn't a blow) through `Player.die()`, as every death does (AGENTS.md rule 6). Nothing is delayed: when the time runs out the body simply has whatever health it has.
- `validate.js`: `press/undying` needs `charge`, `time`; `CONFIG.abilities.undying.floor` above 0.

## Multiplayer

The floor is its holder's own health (the client owns it); the server accepts the press and then accepts that the holder did not die for `time` s plus its slack. Holder only: the flame never protects a teammate, and a fallen teammate is never revived by it.

## Effect

Layered, timed from the press (t = 0) and from a killing blow held (t = k):

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00-0.25 | Ignite | A tall flat flame shape, 1.2 m high, rises over the head: hard-edged tongues in 2 tones with dark inner lines, white at the base | `#f2f6fa` base, `#8fb8dc` tongues, `#0b0d12` inner lines |
| 0.25-`time` | Burn | The flame holds, its tongues swaying; 4 sparks a second lift off its tip | `#8fb8dc` |
| k | Flare | The flame flares to 2.2 m in 0.1 s and a hard ring of blue light bursts from the kneeling body along the floor, 3 m across | `#f2f6fa`, `#8fb8dc` ring |
| k-k+0.6 | Hold | The holder kneels with the sword planted; the health bar's sliver burns blue | `#8fb8dc` |
| last 0.6 s | Gutter | The flame shrinks and gutters so its end is readable | to `#2c5f8a` |
| `time`-+0.3 | Out | The flame goes out in a thin curl of smoke | `#9a958c` |

Budget (Rare class): 3 pooled meshes (flame sheet, floor ring, smoke curl) + 4 sparks a second and 16 at a flare (at most 30 alive; 17 on Normal), 1 effect light (blue, low while it burns, a 0.2 s rise at a flare, intensity × 0.65 on Normal), no ribbon, no impact frame. Peak 0.1 s at a flare. At most one flare a blow, so never past 3 Hz. Reduced motion: the flare grows over 0.2 s instead of 0.1 s.

## Sound

`abilityUnbroken` (new, in `js/data/audio.js`): on the press a body of a flame drawn up (pink noise band-passed sweeping 300 Hz to 1.5 kHz, 0.3 s) over a low held note (sine 110 Hz, held `time` s at low gain, a heartbeat-slow tremolo); on a killing blow held a transient of a deep gong (sine 73 Hz with 2.4 and 3.9 partials, driven, 2 ms attack), a body of the flame roaring up (brown noise low-passed at 600 Hz, 0.4 s), a tail of a long ring (1.5 s).

## Camera

`CONFIG.camera.feel.powers.undying = [2, 0.08]`: on a killing blow held only, a wide kick with the kneel.

## Images

- `img/unbroken-1.webp`: a battered swordsman refusing to fall, a tall blue flame of will burning above their head as a killing blow lands.

# Grave Hound

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Id | `grave-hound` |
| Rarity | Rare (cool blue `#8fb8dc`), 3 levels |
| Kind | Key 3, Summon |
| Trigger | `press`: key 3 pressed with its charge full (20, 18, 16 points) |
| Origin | Kept from js/data/abilities.js: numbers and text unchanged; the green grave-fire becomes black ink and blue fire, the hide shows its ribs, it leaps out of its holder's shadow instead of a fire pool, and its bites leave blue tooth marks. |

## Card

**A hound hunts the boss for {time}.** (7 words, 29 chars)

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): a lean hound's head and forelegs in mid-leap, ribs drawn as three curved lines, one eye a dot.
- Hover loop (1.8 s): the key 3 square lights (0.2 s); a hound leaps up out of a small figure's shadow (0.3 s), runs to the boss's flank and bites twice, each bite leaving a blue mark (1.0 s); it throws its head back in a howl and the boss turns to it; fade.

## Idea

A gaunt spectral hound of the grave leaps out of your shadow and hunts the boss's flank, biting again and again, and howls to turn the boss on itself for a moment. The summon that is all pace: fast, low, always moving round the boss, the companion that makes a solo fight feel like a pack hunt.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'grave-hound', name: 'Grave Hound', rarity: 'rare', key: 'summon',
  text: 'A hound hunts the boss for {time}.',
  power: { when: 'press', then: 'hound' },
  levels: [
    { charge: 20, time: 8, every: 1.2, damage: 16, draw: 2 },
    { charge: 18, time: 10, every: 1.1, damage: 20, draw: 2.5 },
    { charge: 16, time: 12, every: 1, damage: 24, draw: 3 },
  ] },
```

Numbers: after its 0.7 s arrival it bites about 6, 8 and 11 times at levels I-III: about 100, 170 and 265 damage a call, plus 2-3 s of the boss's attention. 20 points at 1-1.4 a second is a hound every 14-20 s, so it is out about half the fight at level III. Unchanged from the shipped entry; it is the summons' measuring stick.

## Engine work

- None for the rule: `press/hound` is in `ABILITY_POWERS`, `hound` in `SUMMONS` and `SUMMON_STRIKERS`, and `CONFIG.abilities.summons.hound` places it.
- Drawing (js/summon-hound.js): the arrival rises from an ink pool in the holder's shadow, not a fire pool; the colours in `VIS.abilityFx.hound` change to the rare palette below; each bite leaves a tooth-mark decal on the boss; the shader's `bone` term draws the ribs brighter.
- Summon pools are built when a player in the run takes the ability (at the pick screen, between fights) and warmed then, never mid-fight; four of a kind at most (one a player).

### Model

- Kept: `tools/blender/hound.py`, packed to `js/baked/hound.js` (`node tools/pack-baked.cjs hound`). Reworked in place: the hide over the ribcage is cut away into five rib bars with gaps between them, the spine shows as a ridge of knuckles, the tail ends in a ragged ink brush tip.
- Look: a lean, long-legged grave hound, all ribs and sinew, its body of black brush ink with blue fire licking along its back and edges, two blue eyes. Nothing like any enemy's dog.
- Height: 1.0 m at the shoulder, 1.6 m nose to tail.
- Material: the summon fresnel shader as now: an ink-dark body (`#0b0d12`, `body` 0.22), bright blue rims (`#8fb8dc`, `rim` 2.6), ribs and teeth in a brighter `bone` term (`#cfe4f2`), eyes and the fire along the spine in white-hot `#f2f6fa`.
- Rig: one rigid piece per joint on pivots (`HOUND_JOINTS`), as now; about 2,500 triangles.
- Animations (all moved by hand in js/summon-hound.js): arrive (it claws up out of the shadow pool and lands at a run, 0.55 s), idle (a low prowl round the boss), run (a gallop above 5 m/s), strike (a lunge with the jaws snapping 30% of the way in, 0.42 s), draw (its head thrown back in a 1.1 s howl), leave (it burns away from the head down, 0.7 s, ash and blue motes falling). It never pops in or out.

## Multiplayer

One summon per holder at a time: a press on key 3 with another summon out sends that one away (its drawn boss is freed). The server owns the hound: it places it, bites for it, and once it has arrived lets it draw the boss's eye for `draw` s (2-3 s), the boss fighting it instead of anyone; it can't be hurt, and an attack begun on it ends on it. It never blocks, pushes or heals a teammate: it has no collision with players and teammates' bodies and blows pass through it. Every browser draws it from the `abilityPower` events.

## Effect

Layered, timed from the press (t = 0) and from each bite (t = b):

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00-0.55 | Arrive | An ink pool spreads in the holder's shadow; the hound claws up out of it and leaps, blue fire catching along its spine; 12 ink drops fly | `#0b0d12` pool, `#8fb8dc` fire, `#f2f6fa` eyes |
| 0.55-`time` | Hunt | It runs to the boss's flank and prowls; blue fire streams back off its spine and tail; 1 mote every 0.09 s | `#8fb8dc` |
| b-b+0.15 | Bite | A lunge; on the snap a crescent of white tooth-marks stamps onto the boss at the bite point, and 8 hard blue sparks spray | `#f2f6fa` marks, `#8fb8dc` sparks |
| b+0.15-b+1.0 | Marks | The tooth-marks fade on the boss | to transparent |
| draw | Howl | Its head thrown back; a thin ring of blue light rises off it | `#8fb8dc` |
| `time`-+0.7 | Leave | It burns away from the head down, ash and blue motes falling | `#9a958c`, `#8fb8dc` |

Budget (Rare summon class): the model + 3 pooled meshes (ink pool, tooth-mark decal, howl ring) + 24 particles at the arrival and 8 a bite (at most 40 alive; 22 on Normal), 1 effect light while striking (blue, 0.2 s a bite, intensity × 0.65 on Normal), no ribbon, no impact frame. Peak 0.15 s a bite. Bites come at most once a second, under 3 Hz. Reduced motion: no change needed.

## Sound

Unchanged: `abilityHound` on the call (a breath of cold fire, a growl, a far bell), `abilityBite` on each bite (the jaws' clack, a tearing snarl, a thump), `abilityHowl` on the draw (a long rising cry over cold wind). The arrival's fire layer is band-passed higher (900 Hz to 2.6 kHz) to sound colder.

## Camera

Unchanged: `CONFIG.camera.feel.powers.hound = [1.4, 0.05]` on the call, `bite = [-0.5, 0.02]` on each bite, `draw = [1.2, 0.03]` on the howl.

# Ink Crows

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Id | `ink-crows` |
| Rarity | Rare (cool blue `#8fb8dc`), 3 levels |
| Kind | Key 3, Summon |
| Trigger | `press`: key 3 pressed with its charge full (18, 16, 15 points) |

## Card

**Ink crows swarm the boss for {time}.** (7 words, 31 chars)

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): five small crow shapes in a ring round a horned head's outline, two ink drops falling from it.
- Hover loop (1.8 s): the key 3 square lights (0.2 s); a stream of black crows pours from a small figure's coat (0.3 s), loops up and rings the boss's head, pecking in quick darts with ink drops splashing (1.0 s); they tighten in front of its face and it swats at them; fade.

## Idea

A murder of crows made of brush ink pours out of your coat and swarms the boss's head: many small, quick pecks instead of one big blow, and a cloud the boss swats at for a moment. It is the summon of steady pressure, and the most "anime" entrance in the set: a black ribbon of birds unspooling from the hero's coat.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'ink-crows', name: 'Ink Crows', rarity: 'rare', key: 'summon',
  text: 'Ink crows swarm the boss for {time}.',
  power: { when: 'press', then: 'crows' },
  levels: [
    { charge: 18, time: 7, every: 0.25, damage: 5, draw: 1.5 },
    { charge: 16, time: 8, every: 0.25, damage: 6, draw: 1.8 },
    { charge: 15, time: 9, every: 0.25, damage: 7, draw: 2 },
  ] },
```

Numbers: after its 0.7 s arrival it pecks 4 times a second: about 25, 29 and 33 pecks, so about 125, 175 and 230 damage a call, in line with the hound (about 100-265) at a slightly lower charge, with 1.5-2 s of the boss's attention. Small pecks add little posture each, so it never staggers the boss on its own. 18 points at 1-1.4 a second is a swarm every 13-18 s.

## Engine work

- New power `press/crows` in `ABILITY_POWERS` (`['charge', 'time', 'every', 'damage', 'draw']`); `crows` joins `SUMMONS`, `SUMMON_STRIKERS` and `ON_ENEMY`, and `fire`'s summon case takes every kind in `SUMMONS` (it names four today).
- `CONFIG.abilities.summons.crows: { gap: 0, flank: 0, speed: 16, height: 0.6, reach: 1.5, head: true }`: a new `head` flag puts its place at the enemy's head (its body's top, the enemy's `height`), so the swarm rings the head and follows it. While it draws the boss, its decoy sits 1 m in front of the boss's face at head height, so the boss swats at the air before it.
- The pecks are emitted to every browser like any strike (`strike` its number), 4 a second; the drawing picks which crow darts in by the peck's number so every client shows the same one. Their sound and light are throttled (below).
- Summon pools are built when a player in the run takes the ability (at the pick screen) and warmed then.

### Model

- File: `tools/blender/ink_crows.py`, packed to `js/baked/ink-crows.js` (a `FILES` entry `'ink-crows': { sources: ['ink_crows'] }` in tools/pack-baked.cjs).
- Look: one crow of black brush ink, ragged wing and tail feathers that end in dry-brush tips, a sharp beak, two blue eyes; the body reads as a single ink stroke at a distance. Twenty-four of them fly at once.
- Size: 0.35 m beak to tail, 0.7 m wingspan.
- Material: the summon fresnel shader: ink-dark body (`#0b0d12`), blue rims on the wing edges (`#8fb8dc`), eyes white-hot (`#f2f6fa`). A vertex weight on the wings (0 at the body, 1 at the tips) lets the vertex shader flap them.
- Rig: none; one mesh of about 300 triangles drawn as one `InstancedMesh` of 24, each crow's place, heading and flap phase set per instance. One draw call for the swarm.
- Animations (in the shader and on the instances): arrive (the crows unspool from the holder's coat in a ribbon, each taking off 25 ms after the last, 0.6 s), idle (a ring 1.6 m round the head, bobbing ±0.4 m, flapping out of step), strike (one crow darts in to the boss and back, 0.2 s), draw (the swarm tightens into a screen before the boss's face, 0.6 s), leave (one by one over 0.6 s each crow bursts into a splash of ink drops that fall and fade). They never pop in or out.

## Multiplayer

One summon per holder at a time: a press on key 3 with another summon out sends that one away. The server owns the swarm: it places it, pecks for it and draws the boss's eye with it for `draw` s (1.5-2 s) after it arrives; it can't be hurt, and an attack begun on it ends on it. The crows fly at the boss's head, never in a teammate's way: no collision, no push, no heal. Every browser draws it from the `abilityPower` events.

## Effect

Layered, timed from the press (t = 0) and from each peck (t = p):

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00-0.60 | Pour | A ribbon of crows unspools from the holder's coat and arcs up to the boss's head; a brush smear of ink trails the stream | `#0b0d12` crows and smear, `#8fb8dc` wing edges |
| 0.60-`time` | Swarm | The ring circles the head; 1 ink drop falls from it every 0.1 s | `#0b0d12`, `#f2f6fa` eyes |
| p-p+0.20 | Peck | One crow darts in; on contact a small flat splash of ink and 2 hard blue sparks | `#0b0d12` splash, `#8fb8dc` sparks |
| draw | Screen | The swarm packs into a flat disc before the face; the boss swats through it | `#0b0d12` |
| `time`-+0.6 | Leave | Crows burst one by one into ink drops that fall and fade | `#0b0d12` to transparent |

Budget (Rare summon class): the model (one instanced mesh of 24) + 2 pooled meshes (the pour smear, the ink splash decal) + ink drops and sparks (at most 40 alive; 22 on Normal), 1 effect light while striking: a low steady blue glow inside the swarm, never pulsed a peck (4 pecks a second would pass 3 Hz). No ribbon besides the smear, no impact frame. Reduced motion: no change needed (no flash). The swarm stays above the boss's shoulders, and the screen at the draw is the one moment it sits before the face, never during a wind-up's last 0.3 s.

## Sound

`abilityCrows` (new, in `js/data/audio.js`) on the call: a transient of a coat snapping open (band-passed noise at 1.5 kHz, 30 ms), a body of many wings beating (pink noise band-passed at 900 Hz with a fast 12 Hz amplitude flutter, 0.6 s), a tail of three harsh caws (sawtooth 420 Hz with a 1.3 partial, band-passed at 1.2 kHz, 0.15 s each, 0.2 s apart). `abilityPeck` on pecks: a dry tick (white noise band-passed at 4 kHz, 8 ms), played at most every 0.25 s with heavy jitter so it reads as a flurry; one caw every 2 s while it swarms.

## Camera

`CONFIG.camera.feel.powers.crows = [0.8, 0.02]` on the call; no kick a peck (4 a second would shake the view); `draw = [1.2, 0.03]` on the screen.

## Images

- `img/ink-crows-1.webp`: a swarm of black brush-ink crows with glowing blue eyes pouring from the swordsman's coat and swirling around a boss's head, ink drops splattering.

A wandering ghost swordsman in a wide straw hat steps in beside you and duels the boss, meeting its first blow with a deflect and a spark and answering with clean, held cuts. It is the summon that fights the way the player fights: a mirror of the game's own deflect-and-counter duel, and the longest hold on the boss's attention among the strikers.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'ronin-shade', name: 'Ronin Shade', rarity: 'rare', key: 'summon',
  text: 'A ghost swordsman duels the boss for {time}.',

  ] },
```

- File: `tools/blender/ronin_shade.py`, packed to `js/baked/ronin-shade.js` (`'ronin-shade': { sources: ['ronin_shade'] }`).
- Look: a lean wandering swordsman in a wide, shallow straw hat that hides the face, a tattered cloak to the shins over a plain wrapped coat, straw sandals, one long single-edged blade and its scabbard. No crest, no hood, no scarf (so it is never mistaken for the player) and nothing an enemy wears.

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| 0.00-0.40 | Dart | A burst of flat flame tongues at the holder's heel and the fox shoots out of it toward the boss | `#8fb8dc` tongues, `#f2f6fa` core |

pool.md:
# Lantern Spirit

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Id | `lantern-spirit` |
| Rarity | Rare (cool blue `#8fb8dc`), 3 levels |
| Kind | Key 3, Summon |
| Trigger | `press`: key 3 pressed with its charge full (18, 17, 16 points) |
| Origin | New |

## Card

**A lantern burns the boss and heals you.** (8 words, 39 chars)

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): a round paper lantern with ribbed lines and two hanging streamers, an almond-shaped flame inside it, a small dot flying off to one side.
- Hover loop (1.8 s): the key 3 square lights (0.2 s); a paper lantern unfolds at a small figure's shoulder (0.3 s); it spits three small blue fireballs at the boss one after another, and with each that lands the figure's bar ticks up (1.1 s); fade.

## Idea

A paper lantern spirit floats at your shoulder, an eye-shaped blue flame inside it, and spits small fireballs at the boss; each that lands warms you a sliver. It is the support summon: it stays with you rather than going to the boss, draws nothing, and turns a long fight into a slow trickle of health for the player who keeps fighting.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'lantern-spirit', name: 'Lantern Spirit', rarity: 'rare', key: 'summon',
  text: 'A lantern burns the boss and heals you.',
  power: { when: 'press', then: 'lantern' },
  levels: [
    { charge: 18, time: 10, every: 1.5, damage: 10, heal: 0.02 },
    { charge: 17, time: 11, every: 1.4, damage: 12, heal: 0.025 },
    { charge: 16, time: 12, every: 1.3, damage: 14, heal: 0.03 },
  ] },
```

Numbers: after its 0.7 s arrival it shoots about 6, 7 and 8 fireballs: about 60, 85 and 115 damage and 12%, 18% and 24% of the holder's bar (14-29 health) a call, a little under one Mending (20-30%) spread over 10-12 s, plus damage. It is the weakest striker on purpose: half its value is the heal. It has no `draw`: it never takes the boss's attention. 18 points at 1-1.4 a second is a lantern every 13-18 s.

## Engine work

- New power `press/lantern` in `ABILITY_POWERS` (`['charge', 'time', 'every', 'damage', 'heal']`, no `draw`); `lantern` joins `SUMMONS`, `SUMMON_STRIKERS` and `ON_ENEMY`.
- `CONFIG.abilities.summons.lantern: { gap: 0, flank: 0, speed: 9, height: 0.6, reach: 18, perch: true, lift: 1.9, shot: 14 }`: a new `perch` flag puts its place beside its holder (`side` m to their right, `lift` m up, trailing them at `speed`), not round the enemy; `reach` is how far it shoots from there (the press `range`).
- Each strike is a shot, not a touch: the fireball flies at `shot` m/s and the engine wounds the boss when it arrives (a fixed delay of distance / `shot`), then emits `abilityPower` `then: 'lantern'` with `heal` set. A shot that finds the boss gone or untouchable heals nothing.
- The heal is the holder's only (`abilityHeal(holder, heal, 'lantern')`), applied where the holder's body is owned.
- `validate.js`: `press/lantern` needs `charge`, `time`, `every`, `damage`, `heal` (a share, at most 1); the summons check allows a `perch` kind with no flank meaning.
- Summon pools are built when a player in the run takes the ability (at the pick screen) and warmed then.

### Model

- File: `tools/blender/lantern_spirit.py`, packed to `js/baked/lantern-spirit.js` (`'lantern-spirit': { sources: ['lantern_spirit'] }`).
- Look: a round paper lantern, slightly squashed, its ribs of dark bamboo showing through the paper; a dark wooden cap and base; three long paper streamers hanging from the base that sway; one tear in its paper. Inside, a single almond-shaped flame like an eye, that turns to look at the boss. No face painted on it.
- Size: 0.6 m tall with cap and base, 0.45 m across; the streamers 0.7 m long.
- Material: ink-dark ribs, cap and base (`#0b0d12`); the paper lit from inside (a blue emissive term `#8fb8dc`, bright at the silhouette, darker across the face so the ribs read); the eye-flame white-hot (`#f2f6fa`). Slots: `frame`, `paper` (glows), `flame` (glows).
- Rig: three rigid pieces (body, flame, streamers on a swing bone each); about 900 triangles.
- Animations (by hand): arrive (it unfolds from a flat folded paper at the holder's shoulder, ribs opening like a fan, then the flame lights, 0.5 s), idle (a slow bob of 8 cm and the streamers swaying; the eye-flame tracks the boss), strike (it puffs out, the paper bulging, and spits a fireball, 0.2 s), leave (the flame gutters to a point and the lantern folds flat and drifts down to the floor as a scrap of paper that fades, 0.6 s). It never pops in or out.

## Multiplayer

One summon per holder at a time: a press on key 3 with another summon out sends that one away. The server owns the lantern's shots on the boss and emits each heal with the shot's event; the holder's browser applies the heal to its own body (the client owns its health) and the server accepts heals up to what it emitted. It heals its holder only, never a teammate. It floats at the holder's shoulder, with no collision, and never blocks or pushes anyone. It draws nothing: the boss never turns to it. Every browser draws it from the `abilityPower` events.

## Effect

Layered, timed from the press (t = 0) and from each shot (t = s):

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00-0.50 | Unfold | The folded paper opens like a fan at the shoulder; the eye-flame lights inside | `#8fb8dc` paper, `#f2f6fa` flame, `#0b0d12` ribs |
| s-s+0.05 | Spit | The paper bulges; a hard flat ring of light at its mouth | `#f2f6fa` |
| s-arrival | Fireball | A small hard-edged fireball, 0.3 m, white core and blue tongues, ink outline, with a short ribbon of flame behind it | `#f2f6fa` core, `#8fb8dc` tongues |
| arrival | Burst | A small flat flame burst on the boss, 0.8 m, 8 sparks | `#8fb8dc`, `#f2f6fa` |
| arrival+0.1 | Warm | A thin blue line runs from the lantern down the holder's arm; the health bar ticks up with a blue sweep | `#8fb8dc` |
| `time`-+0.6 | Leave | The flame gutters; the lantern folds and drifts down | to transparent |

Budget (Rare summon class): the model + 3 pooled meshes (fireball, burst, warm line) + 1 ribbon (the fireball's trail) + 8 sparks a shot and 2 motes a second off the lantern (at most 24 alive; 13 on Normal), 1 effect light while striking (blue, the lantern's own glow, brightening 0.15 s a shot, intensity × 0.65 on Normal), no impact frame. Peak 0.15 s a shot; one every 1.3-1.5 s, under 3 Hz. Reduced motion: no change needed.

## Sound

`abilityLantern` (new, in `js/data/audio.js`) on the call: a transient of paper unfolding (band-passed noise crinkles at 3 kHz, 4 grains in 0.3 s), a body of a candle catching (pink noise band-passed at 600 Hz, 0.3 s), a tail of a soft wind chime (sines 1047, 1319 and 1568 Hz, 0.8 s, staggered). `abilityLanternShot` on each shot: a small puff (brown noise, 60 ms) and a whistle as it flies (sine 1800 Hz gliding to 1200 Hz, 0.2 s); on the heal a single soft chime (sine 784 Hz, 0.3 s), quieter than Mending.

## Camera

`CONFIG.camera.feel.powers.lantern = [0.6, 0]` as it unfolds; no kick a shot.

## Images

- `img/lantern-spirit-1.webp`: a floating paper lantern spirit with a single eye-shaped blue flame inside hovering at the swordsman's shoulder, spitting a small fireball at a boss.

# Bone Archer

| | |

## Card

**A bone archer shoots the boss for {time}.** (8 words, 36 chars)

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): a hooded skull over a tall bow drawn to full, one long arrow line flying off to the right.
- Hover loop (1.8 s): the key 3 square lights (0.2 s); a tall skeleton climbs out of the floor at the card's far edge (0.4 s), draws its great bow and looses three arrows of blue light that streak into the boss (1.0 s); fade.

## Idea

A skeleton archer climbs out of the floor at range and looses glowing arrows into the boss. It barely draws the boss's eye, so it stays out of the fight and lives its whole time: the summon for players who want steady damage without moving the boss around, and the one that shows the arena's scale, its arrows streaking across the whole room.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'bone-archer', name: 'Bone Archer', rarity: 'rare', key: 'summon',
  text: 'A bone archer shoots the boss for {time}.',
  power: { when: 'press', then: 'archer' },
  levels: [
    { charge: 17, time: 9, every: 0.9, damage: 14, draw: 0.5 },
    { charge: 16, time: 10, every: 0.85, damage: 16, draw: 0.6 },
    { charge: 15, time: 11, every: 0.8, damage: 18, draw: 0.7 },
  ] },
```

Numbers: after its 0.7 s arrival it looses about 9, 11 and 13 arrows: about 125, 170 and 230 damage a call, with the hound, at a lower charge because it protects almost nothing: 0.5-0.7 s of the boss's attention, a glance. 17 points at 1-1.4 a second is an archer every 12-17 s.

## Engine work

- New power `press/archer` in `ABILITY_POWERS` (`['charge', 'time', 'every', 'damage', 'draw']`); `archer` joins `SUMMONS`, `SUMMON_STRIKERS` and `ON_ENEMY`.
- `CONFIG.abilities.summons.archer: { gap: 8, flank: 0.9, speed: 6, height: 2.1, reach: 20, rises: true, shot: 40 }`: it rises where it will stand, 8 m off the boss's side away from its holder, and shoots from there. The same `shot` delay as the Lantern Spirit's: each arrow wounds the boss when it arrives (distance / `shot` s after the loose).
- Its decoy while it draws is its own place, so the boss turns toward it for half a second without crossing the room.
- Drawing (js/summon-figures.js): a figure kind `archer` with its `model`, `solid: true` (lit bone), `floor: true` (it climbs out of the floor), a `guard` pose (bow low, an arrow nocked) and a `cry` pose (bow raised to the sky), and one move of its own key poses no enemy uses, `archerLoose` (draw to the cheek, loose, follow through).
- Summon pools are built when a player in the run takes the ability (at the pick screen) and warmed then.

### Model

- File: `tools/blender/bone_archer.py`, packed to `js/baked/bone-archer.js` (`'bone-archer': { sources: ['bone_archer'] }`).
- Look: a tall, narrow skeleton in a torn, hooded mantle that hangs to its knees in strips, a dark skull under the hood with two blue points for eyes, long finger bones, and a great bow taller than itself, of dark wood and bone, its string a line of light. A quiver of arrows of light on its back. Nothing like the game's enemy bowman.
- Height: 2.1 m; the bow 2.2 m.
- Material: the figures' summon shader, lit: bone pale and cold (`#cfe4f2` dimmed), the mantle ink-dark (`#0b0d12`), blue rims (`#8fb8dc`) on the bone edges, eyes, string and arrows white-hot (`#f2f6fa`). Slots: `bone`, `cloth`, `wood`, `light` (glows).
- Rig: one rigid mesh per game bone of js/rig.js's skeleton, the mantle on the cape bones; about 3,000 triangles.
- Animations: arrive (a hand claws up out of the floor, then it climbs out to its full height, 0.7 s), idle (bow low, a slow turn to track the boss), strike (`archerLoose`), draw (bow raised to the sky, 0.6 s), leave (it sinks back into the floor, crumbling from the hood down, 0.7 s). It never pops in or out.

## Multiplayer

One summon per holder at a time: a press on key 3 with another summon out sends that one away. The server owns the archer: it places it, shoots for it and draws the boss's eye with it for `draw` s (0.5-0.7 s) after it arrives; it can't be hurt, and an attack begun on it ends on it. Its arrows fly to the boss only and pass through players: no collision, no push, no heal. Every browser draws it from the `abilityPower` events.

## Effect

Layered, timed from the press (t = 0) and from each loose (t = s):

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00-0.70 | Climb | A crack of blue light opens in the floor; a hand, then the skeleton climbs out; 12 stone chips | `#8fb8dc` crack, `#cfe4f2` bone, `#9a958c` chips |
| s-0.25-s | Draw | The string pulled to the cheek; the arrow's head brightens | `#f2f6fa` |
| s-arrival | Arrow | A thin arrow of light with a hard white streak behind it, 3 m long, across the room | `#f2f6fa` core, `#8fb8dc` edge |
| arrival | Strike | A flat four-point star where it hits and 5 sparks | `#f2f6fa`, `#8fb8dc` |
| draw | Raise | Bow raised; its string flares | `#f2f6fa` |
| `time`-+0.7 | Sink | It crumbles and sinks into the crack, which closes | `#9a958c` |

Budget (Rare summon class): the model + 3 pooled meshes (floor crack, arrow, hit star) + 1 ribbon (the arrow's streak) + 12 chips at the climb and 5 sparks a hit (at most 24 alive; 13 on Normal), 1 effect light while striking (blue-white, on the bow, 0.15 s a loose, intensity × 0.65 on Normal), no impact frame. Peak 0.1 s a hit; an arrow every 0.8-0.9 s, under 3 Hz. Reduced motion: the arrow's streak is shorter (1.5 m). The arrows fly at the boss's body, so they cross the room but never over a player's view for long (0.2 s).

## Sound

`abilityArcher` (new, in `js/data/audio.js`) on the call: a transient of stone cracking (white noise band-passed at 2 kHz, 30 ms), a body of bones and grit climbing (brown noise low-passed at 500 Hz with a dry rattle of short clicks, 0.6 s), a tail of a low wooden creak (sawtooth 90 Hz band-passed at 400 Hz, 0.4 s). `abilityArrow` on each loose: a string's thrum (sine 196 Hz plucked, 0.2 s) and a whistle (band-passed noise sweeping 4 to 2 kHz, 0.2 s); on the hit a dull thock (brown noise, 50 ms) at the boss.

## Camera

`CONFIG.camera.feel.powers.archer = [0.8, 0.02]` as it climbs out; no kick an arrow.

## Images

- `img/bone-archer-1.webp`: a tall skeleton archer in a torn hood rising from the floor at the edge of the arena, drawing a great bow and loosing arrows of blue light at a boss.

**A thunder hawk dives on the boss for {time}.** (9 words, 39 chars)

```js
{ id: 'thunder-hawk', name: 'Thunder Hawk', rarity: 'rare', key: 'summon',
```

### Model

- File: `tools/blender/thunder_hawk.py`, packed to `js/baked/thunder-hawk.js` (`'thunder-hawk': { sources: ['thunder_hawk'] }`).
- Look: a large hawk with long, fingered primaries and a hooked beak, its body an ink-dark silhouette and its feathers drawn as branching lightning lines along every wing edge and down the tail; two blue eyes. The wings' lightning lines are what read at a distance.
- Size: 0.6 m beak to tail, 1.8 m wingspan.

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00-0.60 | Rise | A short jagged bolt up from the holder's raised arm; the hawk climbs out of its end | `#f2f6fa` bolt, `#8fb8dc` lines |
| 0.60-`time` | Circle | It circles high; 1 small spark falls off its wingtips every 0.2 s | `#8fb8dc` |
| d-d+0.35 | Stoop | It dives with wings swept back; a jagged bolt ribbon draws itself behind it from the sky to the boss; radial speed lines round it | `#f2f6fa` core, `#8fb8dc` edge, `#0b0d12` speed lines |
| d+0.35 | Strike | A flat starburst of short forked lines on the boss, 1.6 m, and a scorch ring on the floor under it; 12 sparks | `#f2f6fa`, `#8fb8dc`, `#2a2827` scorch |
| d+0.35-d+0.8 | Fade | The bolt ribbon flickers once and fades | to transparent |
| `time`-+0.6 | Leave | It climbs and thins into a fork of light | `#8fb8dc` to transparent |

Budget (Rare summon class): the model + 3 pooled meshes (starburst, scorch ring, speed-line sheet) + 1 ribbon (the bolt) + 12 sparks a strike and 5 a second circling (at most 30 alive; 17 on Normal), 1 effect light while striking (blue-white, 0.2 s a strike, intensity × 0.65 on Normal), no impact frame. `abilityHawk` (new, in `js/data/audio.js`) on the call: a transient of a crack of static (white noise band-passed at 5 kHz, 15 ms), a body of wings and a hawk's scream (sawtooth 1800 Hz gliding to 1300 Hz, band-passed at 2.2 kHz, 0.4 s), a tail of a far roll of thunder (brown noise low-passed at 200 Hz, 1 s). `abilityStoop` on each dive: a rising wind whistle over the 0.35 s (band-passed noise sweeping 1 to 4 kHz), then the strike's thunderclap (white noise burst 10 ms, a 60 Hz thump driven, 0.3 s), a shorter cousin of `abilityThunder`.

```js

  levels: [
    { charge: 20, time: 6, every: 0.5, damage: 9, draw: 2 },
    { charge: 18, time: 7, every: 0.5, damage: 10, draw: 2.3 },
    { charge: 16, time: 8, every: 0.5, damage: 11, draw: 2.6 },
  ] },
```

Numbers: after its 0.7 s arrival it squeezes twice a second: about 10, 12 and 14 squeezes, so about 95, 125 and 160 damage a call, below the hound for the same charge, paid back by the surest damage of any summon (it can't be outrun or left behind) and 2-2.6 s of the boss's attention. 20 points at 1-1.4 a second is a serpent every 14-20 s.

## Engine work

- New power `press/serpent` in `ABILITY_POWERS` (`['charge', 'time', 'every', 'damage', 'draw']`); `serpent` joins `SUMMONS`, `SUMMON_STRIKERS` and `ON_ENEMY`.
- `CONFIG.abilities.summons.serpent: { gap: 0.8, flank: 1.2, speed: 40, height: 1.6, reach: 3, rises: true, coil: true }`: a new `coil` flag keeps it on its enemy. Its body is drawn round the enemy's own place each frame; its place in the engine (where its head stands, and its decoy while it draws) is `gap` m off the enemy's side at `flank`, followed at `speed` so it never falls behind. The squeezes never stop or slow the boss: it moves, turns and attacks as usual.
- Drawing: a new `js/summon-coil.js`: the body as a chain of rigid segments laid along a helix round the enemy (radius the enemy's `radius` + 0.2 m, three turns rising to 60% of its `height`), the head on its own pivot.
- Summon pools are built when a player in the run takes the ability (at the pick screen) and warmed then.

### Model

- File: `tools/blender/mire_serpent.py`, packed to `js/baked/mire-serpent.js` (`'mire-serpent': { sources: ['mire_serpent'] }`).
- Look: a long eel-like serpent of black water, smooth and glossy, with a ridge of tall, thin, hard-edged spines down its back and two long fin-frills behind its head; a blunt, eyeless head with a wide mouth and one row of needle teeth; its spines and fin edges glow blue.
- Size: about 6 m long, 0.35 m thick at its widest; its head rises to 2.6 m.
- Material: the summon fresnel shader: an ink-dark glossy body (`#0b0d12`, with a cold specular band so it reads as wet), blue rims and spines (`#8fb8dc`), the spine tips and teeth white-hot (`#f2f6fa`).
- Rig: twelve body segments plus head and jaw, each a rigid piece placed along the helix by the drawing code (no skeleton); about 2,400 triangles in all.
- Animations: arrive (a black pool opens under the boss, and the serpent rises from it and winds up the boss's body from the feet, 0.7 s), idle (the coils slide slowly round the body; the head sways beside the boss), strike (a squeeze: the coils tighten 10% and the spines flare, 0.2 s, then ease), draw (the head rears up in front of the boss with its mouth open and frills spread, 1 s), leave (the coils unwind downward and pour back into the pool as water, which closes, 0.7 s). It never pops in or out.

## Multiplayer

One summon per holder at a time: a press on key 3 with another summon out sends that one away. The server owns the serpent: it places it, squeezes for it and draws the boss's eye with its head for `draw` s (2-2.6 s) after it arrives; it can't be hurt, and an attack begun on it ends on it. It is wrapped round the boss only, with no collision: it never blocks, pushes or heals a teammate, and teammates strike the boss through its coils. Every browser draws it from the `abilityPower` events.

## Effect

Layered, timed from the press (t = 0) and from each squeeze (t = h):

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00-0.20 | Pool | A flat black pool opens on the floor under the boss, 1 m wider than it, hard edge, blue rim | `#0b0d12` pool, `#8fb8dc` rim |
| 0.20-0.70 | Rise | The serpent rises from it and winds up the body; 14 water droplets thrown off | `#0b0d12` body, `#8fb8dc` spines, `#f2f6fa` droplets |
| h-h+0.20 | Squeeze | The coils tighten; the spines flare white-blue along their length; 4 droplets squeezed out | `#f2f6fa` spine tips, `#8fb8dc` |
| draw | Rear | The head rears with frills spread; a ring of blue light round its neck | `#8fb8dc` |
| `time`-+0.7 | Leave | The coils unwind and pour back into the pool, which shrinks and closes | `#0b0d12` to transparent |

Budget (Rare summon class): the model (the segments drawn as one instanced mesh) + 2 pooled meshes (the pool decal, the neck ring) + 14 droplets at the rise and 4 a squeeze (at most 30 alive; 17 on Normal), 1 effect light while striking: a low steady blue glow from the spines, never pulsed per squeeze (two a second is safe, but a steady light reads better). No ribbon, no impact frame. Reduced motion: the spines brighten without the flare. The coils stay below the boss's shoulders, never over its arms or weapon, so every wind-up stays readable.

## Sound

`abilitySerpent` (new, in `js/data/audio.js`) on the call: a transient of a deep plunge (sine 70 Hz with a 2.4 partial, 2 ms attack, 0.3 s), a body of water rising and pouring (band-passed noise sweeping 300 Hz to 1.2 kHz, 0.6 s, with a gurgle of 8 Hz amplitude wobble), a tail of a low wet hiss (pink noise high-passed at 2 kHz, 0.5 s). `abilityCoil` on each squeeze: a creak of pressure (sawtooth 65 Hz, low-passed at 250 Hz, 0.15 s) at low gain, every other squeeze only, so it reads as a slow pulse. On the draw a long hiss from the open mouth (white noise band-passed at 5 kHz, 0.8 s).

## Camera

`CONFIG.camera.feel.powers.serpent = [1.6, 0.06]` as it rises; no kick a squeeze; `draw = [1.2, 0.03]` on the rear.

## Images

- `img/mire-serpent-1.webp`: a long eel-like serpent of black water with glowing blue spines rising from a pool and coiling around a boss's body.

# Puppet Knight

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Id | `puppet-knight` |
| Rarity | Rare (cool blue `#8fb8dc`), 3 levels |
| Kind | Key 3, Summon |
| Trigger | `press`: key 3 pressed with its charge full (20, 18, 16 points) |
| Origin | New |

## Card

**A puppet knight fights the boss for {time}.** (8 words, 38 chars)

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): a jointed knight figure with round joints, five thin string lines running up from its head, hands and knees to a small cross bar at the top.
- Hover loop (1.8 s): the key 3 square lights and a small figure raises its fingers (0.2 s); a wooden knight drops from above on glowing strings and lands in a crouch (0.4 s); it chops at the boss twice in jerky snapping poses, the strings pulling taut each time (1.0 s); fade.

## Idea

A wooden knight marionette drops from above on glowing strings that run up into the dark and down to your raised fingers, and fights the boss in jerky, snapping blows. You see it fight on its strings, as if you were working it. It is the summon that holds the boss longest among the strikers, a sturdy decoy with an unsettling, theatrical way of moving that no enemy shares.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'puppet-knight', name: 'Puppet Knight', rarity: 'rare', key: 'summon',
  text: 'A puppet knight fights the boss for {time}.',
  power: { when: 'press', then: 'puppet' },
  levels: [
    { charge: 20, time: 10, every: 1.3, damage: 20, draw: 3 },
    { charge: 18, time: 11, every: 1.2, damage: 24, draw: 3.5 },
    { charge: 16, time: 12, every: 1.1, damage: 28, draw: 4 },
  ] },
```

Numbers: after its 0.7 s arrival it strikes about 7, 8 and 10 times: about 140, 195 and 280 damage a call, the top of the rare summons with the hound and the Ronin Shade, and 3-4 s of the boss's attention. 20 points at 1-1.4 a second is a knight every 14-20 s, so at level III it is out more than half the fight.

## Engine work

- New power `press/puppet` in `ABILITY_POWERS` (`['charge', 'time', 'every', 'damage', 'draw']`); `puppet` joins `SUMMONS`, `SUMMON_STRIKERS` and `ON_ENEMY`.
- `CONFIG.abilities.summons.puppet: { gap: 1.2, flank: 1, speed: 7, height: 2, reach: 1.8, rises: true, drop: 6 }`: it arrives where it will stand (`rises`), dropping from `drop` m above in the arrival time instead of climbing out of the floor.
- Drawing (js/summon-figures.js): a figure kind `puppet` with its `model`, `solid: true` (lit wood), a `guard` pose (sword up, limbs hanging slack) and a `cry` pose (arms flung wide, head lolled back), and two `moves` of its own key poses no enemy uses, `puppetChop` (an overhead chop) and `puppetSpin` (a full-body turning cut). Its poses are snapped through with an overshoot and settle (a new `snap` easing on the figure), so it moves like a marionette. Five string lines (one `LineSegments` mesh) run from its head, hands and knees up 12 m into the dark; while it arrives a sixth line runs down to the holder's hand.
- Large summons fade to 40% when they stand between a viewer's camera and the boss (drawing only, per browser), so no friend loses a boss's wind-up behind it.
- Summon pools are built when a player in the run takes the ability (at the pick screen) and warmed then.

### Model

- File: `tools/blender/puppet_knight.py`, packed to `js/baked/puppet-knight.js` (`'puppet-knight': { sources: ['puppet_knight'] }`).
- Look: a life-size marionette of a knight carved in dark wood, ball joints showing at the shoulders, elbows, hips and knees, a cracked great helm with a narrow visor slit, a carved surcoat with chipped paint, a wooden sword with a nicked edge and a small round wooden buckler. Brass screw-eyes at the head, hands and knees where the strings tie on. No crest or emblem.
- Height: 2.0 m.
- Material: the figures' summon shader, lit: dark-stained wood (`#2a2118`, near ink) for the limbs and armour, the ball joints and screw-eyes glowing blue (`#8fb8dc`), the helm's crack and visor slit white-hot (`#f2f6fa`). Slots: `wood`, `paint`, `joint` (glows), `crack` (glows).
- Rig: one rigid mesh per game bone of js/rig.js's skeleton (a marionette is already rigid parts); about 3,200 triangles.
- Animations: arrive (it drops from 6 m on taut strings and lands in a crouch with a wooden clatter, 0.7 s), idle (it hangs slightly off the floor, limbs swaying on slack strings), strike (`puppetChop`, `puppetSpin`, the strings jerking taut on each), draw (arms flung wide and head lolled back, 1 s), leave (the strings go slack one by one and snap upward; it collapses into a heap of parts, which sinks into its shadow, 0.8 s). It never pops in or out.

## Multiplayer

One summon per holder at a time: a press on key 3 with another summon out sends that one away. The server owns the knight: it places it, strikes for it and draws the boss's eye with it for `draw` s (3-4 s) after it arrives; it can't be hurt, and an attack begun on it ends on it. Its strings run to the sky and, only while it arrives, to its own holder's hand; they never touch, link or slow a teammate, and have no collision. The knight never blocks, pushes or heals a teammate. Every browser draws it from the `abilityPower` events.

## Effect

Layered, timed from the press (t = 0) and from each blow (t = h):

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00-0.20 | Strings | Five lines of light draw down out of the dark above the boss's flank; a sixth runs from the holder's raised fingers up to the same point | `#8fb8dc` lines, `#f2f6fa` cores |
| 0.20-0.70 | Drop | The knight drops on them and lands in a crouch; a ring of dust and 10 wood splinters | `#2a2118` wood, `#9a958c` dust |
| 0.70-1.20 | Thread | The line to the holder's hand fades to nothing; the five to the sky stay at 60% | to transparent |
| h-h+0.12 | Blow | A flat arc follows its sword, 2 m, ink outline, a hard white core; the strings flash taut | `#f2f6fa` core, `#8fb8dc` edge, `#0b0d12` outline |
| h+0.12-h+0.40 | Hang | 6 sparks and 3 wood chips at the contact | `#8fb8dc`, `#2a2118` |
| `time`-+0.8 | Collapse | Strings slacken and snap away upward; the heap sinks | to transparent |

Budget (Rare summon class): the model + 3 pooled meshes (the string lines as one `LineSegments`, the blow arc, the dust ring) + 10 splinters at the landing and 9 a blow (at most 30 alive; 17 on Normal), 1 effect light while striking (blue, on its joints, 0.15 s a blow, intensity × 0.65 on Normal), no ribbon, no impact frame. Peak 0.12 s a blow; one every 1.1-1.3 s, under 3 Hz. Reduced motion: the strings don't flash taut. The strings are thin (2 px at most) and stand clear of the boss's body, so they never cover a wind-up.

## Sound

`abilityPuppet` (new, in `js/data/audio.js`) on the call: a transient of strings snapping taut (a plucked sine at 330 Hz with a fast glide up a fifth, 0.1 s), a body of a wooden clatter as it lands (8 short knocks band-passed at 800 Hz over 0.2 s), a tail of a slow creak of wood (sawtooth 110 Hz band-passed at 500 Hz, 0.5 s). `abilityPuppetBlow` on each blow: the strings' twang (sine 440 Hz plucked, 0.15 s) and a hard wooden thwack (band-passed noise at 1.2 kHz, 40 ms, with a 120 Hz thump).

## Camera

`CONFIG.camera.feel.powers.puppet = [1.4, 0.05]` as it lands; no kick a blow; `draw = [1.2, 0.03]` on the cry.

## Images

- `img/puppet-knight-1.webp`: a jointed wooden knight marionette with a cracked helm fighting a boss, glowing blue strings running from its joints up into the dark and to the swordsman's raised fingers.

**An ash bear mauls the boss for {time}.** (8 words, 33 chars)

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): a bear reared on its hind legs, one forepaw raised with three claw lines, the outline broken into plates.

A huge bear of packed grey ash and embers rises beside the boss, rears up and mauls it with slow, heavy swipes. It is the summon of weight: few blows, each the size of a heavy attack, each one a moment, and a body big enough that the boss has to turn and face it. It costs the most charge of any summon.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'ash-bear', name: 'Ash Bear', rarity: 'rare', key: 'summon',
  text: 'An ash bear mauls the boss for {time}.',
  power: { when: 'press', then: 'bear' },
```

- New power `press/bear` in `ABILITY_POWERS` (`['charge', 'time', 'every', 'damage', 'draw']`); `bear` joins `SUMMONS`, `SUMMON_STRIKERS` and `ON_ENEMY`.

### Model

- File: `tools/blender/ash_bear.py`, packed to `js/baked/ash-bear.js` (`'ash-bear': { sources: ['ash_bear'] }`).
- Look: a massive bear of packed grey ash, its hide made of thick overlapping plates like cracked cooling slag, blue embers glowing in the seams between them; a heavy head with a short muzzle and small blue eyes; long black claws that shed ash. Its shoulders hump high; its outline is broken into plates so it reads as made, not alive.
- Height: 1.6 m at the shoulder on all fours, 3.2 m reared.
- Material: the summon shader, lit: ash plates (`#9a958c`) over a charred ink-dark body showing in the seams (`#2a2827`), the seams' embers blue (`#8fb8dc`) with white-hot cores (`#f2f6fa`), claws ink (`#0b0d12`). Slots: `ash`, `char`, `ember` (glows).

One summon per holder at a time: a press on key 3 with another summon out sends that one away. The server owns the bear: it places it, swipes for it and draws the boss's eye with it for `draw` s (3-4 s) after it arrives; it can't be hurt, and an attack begun on it ends on it. It stands on the boss's far side with no collision: it never blocks, pushes or heals a teammate, and fades for any player whose view of the boss it would cover. Every browser draws it from the `abilityPower` events.

## Effect

Layered, timed from the press (t = 0) and from each swipe's landing (t = h; its wind-up, the rear, starts 0.6 s before):

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00-0.70 | Rise | A mound of ash heaves up and breaks; the bear rises out of it shedding ash in hard flakes; its seams light up blue from the feet | `#9a958c` ash, `#8fb8dc` seams |
| h-0.6-h | Rear | It rears; the seams brighten as it climbs | `#f2f6fa` seam cores |

| h+0.15-h+0.6 | Fall | 16 ash chunks and 8 blue embers fall from the impact; a dust ring on the floor | `#9a958c`, `#8fb8dc` |
| draw | Roar | It rears and roars; a flat ring of ash pushes out from its feet (drawn only, it moves no one) | `#9a958c` |
| `time`-+0.8 | Leave | It collapses into ash that blows away | to transparent |

Budget (Rare summon class): the model + 3 pooled meshes (claw arcs, dust ring, ash mound) + 1 ribbon (the claws' ash) + 24 particles a swipe (at most 40 alive with the rise; 22 on Normal), 1 effect light while striking (blue, 0.25 s a swipe, intensity × 0.65 on Normal), no impact frame. Peak 0.15 s a swipe; one every 1.8-2 s. Reduced motion: no change needed (no flash).

# Glass Mantis

| | |
| --- | --- |

| Rarity | Rare (cool blue `#8fb8dc`), 3 levels |

## Card

**A glass mantis slices the boss for {time}.** (8 words, 37 chars)

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): a mantis seen side-on, standing tall, its two long scythe forelegs crossed in an X in front of it, its body drawn in faceted straight lines.
- Hover loop (1.8 s): the key 3 square lights (0.2 s); a crystal shard stabs up from the floor beside the boss and unfolds into a tall glass mantis (0.4 s); it scissors both blades through the boss, quick, quick, a thin white cut line hanging each time (1.0 s); fade.

## Idea

A tall mantis of clear glass, outlined in ink, unfolds from a crystal shard beside the boss and slices it with both scythe-arms in quick scissor cuts. It is the precise, fast summon: the most blows of any striker in a short time, each one a clean, thin line that hangs for a breath, and it shatters when its time ends.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'glass-mantis', name: 'Glass Mantis', rarity: 'rare', key: 'summon',
  text: 'A glass mantis slices the boss for {time}.',
  power: { when: 'press', then: 'mantis' },
  levels: [
    { charge: 18, time: 7, every: 0.8, damage: 16, draw: 1.5 },
    { charge: 17, time: 8, every: 0.75, damage: 18, draw: 1.7 },
    { charge: 16, time: 9, every: 0.7, damage: 20, draw: 1.9 },
```

- New power `press/mantis` in `ABILITY_POWERS` (`['charge', 'time', 'every', 'damage', 'draw']`); `mantis` joins `SUMMONS`, `SUMMON_STRIKERS` and `ON_ENEMY`.
- `CONFIG.abilities.summons.mantis: { gap: 1.3, flank: 1.1, speed: 9, height: 2.4, reach: 2, rises: true }`: it rises where it will stand, on the boss's far side away from its holder.
- Drawing: a beast in `js/summon-beasts.js` (shared with the hound, the fox, the hawk, the bear and the owl). Its glass is drawn after the opaque pass with its ink outline drawn solid, so it reads against any floor.
