# The Seven

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Id | `the-seven` |
| Rarity | Story (scarf crimson `#b3262e`, oath gold `#e8c46a`), 1 level, never offered in a pick |
| Kind | Key 3, Summon, kept for good |
| Trigger | `press`: key 3 with its charge full (24 points) |
| Origin | New |
| Given | Chapter 6, The Church in the Pass, the painted faces |

## Card

**The Seven rise and strike the boss.** (7 words, 35 chars)

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): seven small hooded shapes in a ring seen from above, each a plain oval face with two dots, one open hand drawn at the ring's centre.
- Hover loop (2.0 s): the key cap "3" lights crimson (0.2 s); seven hooded figures rise in a ring round a boss silhouette (0.4 s); they strike one after another, a gold ring off each palm, going round the circle (0.8 s); all seven raise their palms, then strike together, the brighter frame (0.3 s); they fade upward (0.3 s).

## Idea

In the log church in the pass, the founders painted their own faces on the wall. Pressed, seven tall hooded figures of gold light rise in a ring round the boss, each wearing one of those flat painted faces, and strike it with open hands one after another, going round the circle, then raise their palms together and strike all at once. They carry no weapons: an open hand was their oath. It is the biggest summon in the game, a ring of seven, and its last beat is a moment the whole party sees coming.

## Where it's given

The first time the player walks before the church wall where the seven faces are painted, the faces turn, slowly, to follow them, and a faint gold light rises in their painted eyes. The key 3 cap lights crimson with the ability's name, already full, as the player passes the last face. Nothing pauses, the camera stays free and no one speaks; the faces keep watching the player for as long as they stay in the church, and go still when they leave.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'the-seven', name: 'The Seven', rarity: 'story', key: 'summon',
  story: { chapter: 6, place: 'The Church in the Pass, the painted faces' },
  text: 'The Seven rise and strike the boss.',
  power: { when: 'press', then: 'seven' },
  levels: [
    { charge: 24, time: 9, every: 1, damage: 24, draw: 3 },
  ] },
```

Numbers: nine beats, one every `every` s: beats 1-7 each founder in turn (7 × 24 = 168), beat 8 they gather (no blow: the party's cue), beat 9 all together, one blow of `damage` × `CONFIG.abilities.powers.seven.together` (3) = 72. So 240 a press for 24 points, 10 a point, plus the first 3 s of the boss's attention drawn off the holder (a free string, about 60-90). Key 3 fills every 20-25 s: three or four presses a fight, 720-960 on the boss plus the draws. Over the floor (8.4), never a fight won by it.

## Engine work

- New `press/seven`: `['charge', 'time', 'every', 'damage', 'draw']`, a summon of a new kind, `seven`, in `ON_ENEMY`. It is the holder's one summon while out (the slot rule: another kind's call waits).
- Seven figures, not one body: they stand in a ring `CONFIG.abilities.summons.seven = { gap: 2.4, count: 7, height: 2.6, rises: true }` round the enemy's body, evenly spaced, the first opposite the holder; they rise where they stand (no run) and turn with the enemy, keeping the ring.
- Beats: beat n falls at 0.6 s (the pose) + `CONFIG.abilities.summons.arrive` + (n - 1) × `every` after the press (1.3 s, 2.3 s, ... 9.3 s); beat n ≤ `count` is founder n striking (`damage`, a power's blow: it never counts toward `hits`, a counter or a crack, and sets off no power); beat `count` + 1 is the gather; beat `count` + 2 is the together blow (`damage` × `together`). `time` must equal `every` × (`count` + 2); `validate.js` checks it, and that `draw` ≤ `time`.
- Draw: for `draw` s the enemy fights the founder it faces (the decoy rule the twin's draw uses), a body of `height` m.
- Given by the level as Scarlet Draw is: `giveAbility: { id: 'the-seven', trigger: [...] }` along the painted wall (`js/levels/the-church.js`); the faces' turning is a lore `scene` that plays for the player near it.
- `validate.js`: `seven` needs every number above, `damage` and `draw` set.

## Multiplayer

The press is checked by the server as every press is; it raises the ring and resolves every beat and the draw on its own enemy. Founders strike enemies only, have no collision with players and revive no one; the draw only takes the boss's attention for 3 s, which spares whichever player it was on. Played together, each player is given it at the wall and holds their own ring; two rings on one boss stand at different `gap`s (2.4 and 3.4 m) so they never stand inside each other.

## Model

`tools/blender/seven_founder.py`: one figure, used seven times. A tall hooded figure 2.6 m high in a long plain robe that ends in a ragged hem instead of feet, both hands bare and open, no weapon. The face is a flat oval panel set in the hood, painted in a simple folk style: round eyes, straight brows, a line for a mouth, two red cheek marks; the seven faces differ only by small marks (a beard line, a braid, a scar, a lined brow, round spectacles of paint, a younger face, an older one), all on one 7-tile face atlas chosen per figure. About 1.5k triangles. Material: the robe is emissive oath gold with dark ink fold lines and a crimson lining showing at the hood and sleeves; the face panel is unlit painted wood colour so it reads as paint, not light. Rig: root, spine, head and two arms (upper, fore, hand), the same bones on all seven. Animations: `rise` (up out of the floor from the hem, a seam of gold climbing, 0.7 s), `idle` (a slow hover, the hem rippling), `strike` (one open palm thrust, 0.35 s), `gather` (both palms raised high, 0.8 s), `together` (both palms driven in, 0.3 s), `fade` (dissolving upward into gold motes from the hem, 0.8 s). Baked to `js/baked/`; fourteen in the pool (two rings), warmed at load. Seen in the game round a boss before it ships.

## Effect

Timed from the press (t = 0):

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00-0.60 | Anticipation | Upper-body pose: the holder's off hand raised, palm open toward the boss, held; seven small gold marks light in a ring on the floor round the boss, one after another; the world dims 20% | `#e8c46a` marks |
| 0.60-1.30 | Rise | The seven founders rise from their marks, hem first, a seam of gold climbing each; their painted faces come up last, already turned to the boss | `#e8c46a` robe, `#b3262e` lining, `#0b0b0f` ink folds |
| 1.30-7.30 | In turn | Every second one founder strikes, going round the ring: an open palm thrust and a flat gold shock ring off the palm into the boss, 10 hard sparks, the struck founder's face lit a moment | `#e8c46a` ring, `#fff3dc` sparks |
| 8.30 | Gather | All seven raise both palms; a thin gold line joins their hands round the ring and tightens | `#e8c46a` line |
| 9.30 | Peak (together) | All seven palms drive in; seven shock rings converge on the boss and meet in one gold burst of 40 shards. **The impact frame**, ink and white with gold and crimson kept | `#fff3dc` burst, `#e8c46a` rings, `#b3262e` shard edges |
| 9.30-10.30 | Fade | The founders dissolve upward into gold motes, faces last | `#e8c46a` to transparent |

Budget (Story class): 7 founder models + 5 pooled meshes (floor mark ring, shock ring reused, gather line, burst, seam card) = 12 meshes, 10 sparks a strike + 40 at the burst + 50 motes at the fade = 100 particles alive at most (55 on Normal), 2 effect lights (a steady warm light at the ring's centre for the whole 9 s, never pulsing per strike; the burst's; × 0.65 on Normal), 1 ribbon (the gather line), 1 impact frame at t = 9.30. Peak 0.3 s at the burst; the in-turn strikes are one a second, at summon weight. The founders stand 2.4 m off the boss's body, and any founder within 1.5 m of its weapon during a wind-up goes 50% translucent. Reduced motion: the impact frame becomes a 30% darken, no shake.

## Sound

New `abilitySeven`: the rise is a low choir drone (sine partials at 98, 147 and 196 Hz, swelling 0.7 s) with a wooden creak under it (a short low-passed noise grain, 0.2 s). Each strike in turn is a hand clap (white noise burst, band-passed at 1.2 kHz, 30 ms) over a soft frame-drum hit (sine 90 to 60 Hz, 0.2 s) and one note of a rising seven-note scale (196, 220, 247, 262, 294, 330, 370 Hz, 0.5 s each), so the ring plays a climbing tune. The gather holds the seventh note; the together blow is all seven notes at once as a chord with a heavy clap and a deep boom (sine 50 to 32 Hz, 0.8 s). Tail: the chord fading with long reverb (2 s).

## Camera

`CONFIG.camera.feel.powers.seven = [3.0, 0.12]` at the together blow; `draw = [1.2, 0.03]` kept at the rise. No kick for the strikes in turn.

## Images

- `img/the-seven-1.webp`: seven tall hooded figures with flat painted folk-art faces and robes of ember-gold light rising in a ring around a boss in the snow, raising open palms.
- `img/the-seven-2.webp`: a dark log church in a snowy mountain pass with seven painted faces on its wall, faintly glowing.
- `img/the-seven-3.webp`: the Seven striking all together, seven golden open-hand shock rings converging on the boss.

pool.md:
# Bell of Waking

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Id | `bell-of-waking` |
| Rarity | Story (scarf crimson `#b3262e`, oath gold `#e8c46a`), 1 level, never offered in a pick |
| Kind | Key 4, Ultimate, kept for good |
| Trigger | `press`: key 4 with its charge full (48 points) |
| Origin | New |
| Given | Chapter 14, The Still Mere, given by Ysolde |

## Card

**The Bell falls, tolls, and calls the boss down.** (9 words, 47 chars)

- Icon (48×48 line drawing): a large bell seen from the side with one crack running down from its shoulder, a small kneeling figure beneath it, two curved toll lines on each side.
- Hover loop (2.0 s): the key cap "4" lights crimson (0.2 s); a huge bell outline falls from the top of the card over a boss silhouette (0.4 s); it tolls, a ring rolls out to the card's edges and the card drains to black and white but for the gold bell (0.2 s); the boss sinks to one knee under it (0.5 s); it tolls again and bursts into gold pieces, the brighter frame (0.2 s); colour comes back (0.5 s).

## Idea

The last gift, and the biggest moment in the game. Pressed, the ghost of the cracked Bell of Waking falls out of the sky over the boss, huge and gold, and tolls once: a ring of sound rolls across the whole arena, the world drains to ink but for the bell's gold and the red scarf, the falling ash stops in the air, and the boss is called down to one knee, as the founders' law says a crown must answer whoever rings. Two seconds later it tolls again and shatters into gold over the kneeling boss. It is the only technique that stops the world, and it is given right before the fight that needs it.

## Where it's given

On the white bough above the Still Mere, Ysolde waits by the first bonfire with the small bell she cast on the road. The first time the player comes within a few metres of her, she lifts it and rings it once over the water: a thin clear note that rolls out across the mere, the ash nearby hangs still for a breath, and the key 4 cap lights crimson with the ability's name, already full. Nothing pauses and the camera stays the player's; she says nothing unless the player presses Talk, and her lines stay as they are. The ice below, and whatever waits on it, is the first place to ring it.

## Data

```js
{ id: 'bell-of-waking', name: 'Bell of Waking', rarity: 'story', key: 'ultimate',
  story: { chapter: 14, place: 'The Still Mere, given by Ysolde' },
  text: 'The Bell falls, tolls, and calls the boss down.',
  power: { when: 'press', then: 'bellToll' },
  levels: [
    { charge: 48, time: 2, damage: 480 },
  ] },
```

Numbers: 480 at the second toll, as much as a Finishing Blow on a boss and the biggest single power blow in the game, plus `time` s of a boss on one knee that can't act (a free light string and heavy, about 90-130). About 580 for 48 points, 12 a point, the highest of Story's four and well over the floor (8.4). Key 4 fills every 45-50 s, so two tolls a fight: about 1150 on a boss of 1600-3500 health, a third to two thirds of a bar with everything else the player lands in the kneel. It turns the fight; it can't end one alone (the second toll never kills through a phase change).

## Engine work

- New `press/bellToll`: `['charge', 'time', 'damage']`, in `ON_ENEMY` (the locked enemy, else the nearest within `CONFIG.abilities.press.range`); a `running` entry with two beats.
- First toll, 1.0 s after the press: the enemy gets a new hold timer `kneel` = `time`: it plays its kneel (a held stagger pose; an enemy with no kneel clip uses its stagger, frozen at the low point), makes no attack, turns and moves nowhere. The shared hold rest applies (`CONFIG.abilities.holdRest`, 3 s, see Heaven's Lance): an enemy in its rest isn't knelt; the bell still falls and tolls and the second toll still lands. Kneeling is a hold, not a crack: it opens no Finishing Blow and fills no posture.
- Second toll, at the kneel's end (1.0 + `time` s): `damage` to the enemy as a power's blow (it never counts toward `hits`, a counter or a crack, and sets off no power). Like the Finishing Blow's `bossCap` rule, it never leaves a boss past a phase change in one blow: it stops at the phase line.
- The world: the ink grade from World of Ink (one uniform on the output pass) with gold `#e8c46a` and crimson `#b3262e` left in colour, from the first toll to 0.4 s after the second, for every player within `powerNear` (the holder at full, teammates at half); the world's falling ash freezes for the same span (its time uniform held, no new particles).
- Given by the level: `giveAbility: { id: 'bell-of-waking', trigger: [...] }` round Ysolde's place on the white bough (`js/levels/still-mere.js`), with her ringing as a lore `scene` that plays for the player near it.
- `validate.js`: `bellToll` needs `charge`, `time` and `damage`.

## Multiplayer

The press is checked by the server as every press is; it runs both tolls, the kneel and the blow on its own enemy (the server owns the boss's movement). Enemies only: a teammate under the bell is untouched and sees it pass round them; the grade and the frozen ash are drawn for them at half strength, never slowing or moving them. Played together, the story gives each player their own Bell; the hold rest keeps a party's Bells from chaining a boss into an endless kneel, and the impact frame's one-a-second gate keeps four tolls from flashing together.

## Model

`tools/blender/ghost_bell.py`: a great bronze bell 8 m tall and 7 m across the lip, the old tall shape with a heavy waist, a thick sound bow and a crown of six loops on top, plain bands round the shoulder and the lip and a band of raised marks between them (abstract shapes, no letters). One crack runs from the shoulder down past the waist, its edges chipped. About 3k triangles. A second export, `ghost_bell_shards`, is the same bell pre-broken along the crack into 28 pieces, each with its own pivot packed into a vertex attribute so the shatter runs in the shader (one mesh, one draw call). Material: a ghost shader, translucent gold `#e8c46a` at 55% with a white-hot fresnel rim, the crack emissive `#fff3dc`, a black ink outline from an inverted hull, and dark bronze `#3a2a12` showing in the marks. No skeleton: it falls, hangs, swings a little at each toll and breaks. Baked to `js/baked/`; two of each in the pool, warmed at load. Seen in the game over a boss before it ships.

## Effect

Timed from the press (t = 0):

| t | Layer | Look | Colour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00-1.00 | Anticipation | Upper-body pose: the off hand raised open to the sky, held; the world dims 20%; a gold ring opens in the clouds over the boss and the ghost bell comes down through it, slowly, then fast, its crack glowing | `#e8c46a` bell, `#fff3dc` crack, `#0b0b0f` ink |
| 1.00 | First toll (the call) | The bell stops 3 m above the boss's head and swings once; a white toll ring rolls out flat across the floor of the whole arena, with a thin wall of heat-shimmer standing up from it; behind the ring the world drains to ink and paper, only gold and the crimson scarf keep colour; the ash stops mid-air; the boss is driven to one knee | `#fff3dc` ring, `#0b0b0f` / `#e9e4d8` world, `#e8c46a`, `#b3262e` |
| 1.00-3.00 | Kneel | The boss kneels under the hanging bell, which sways and hums; the frozen ash hangs; the crack spreads down the bell in short jumps, gold light leaking from it in thin rays; the holder's scarf moves, nothing else does | `#e8c46a` rays, `#fff3dc` crack |
| 3.00 | Peak (second toll) | The bell tolls and shatters: 28 gold pieces burst outward, a white shockwave runs across the arena floor, 60 hard gold shards. **The impact frame**, ink and white with gold and crimson kept | `#fff3dc` wave, `#e8c46a` pieces, `#b3262e` scarf |
| 3.00-4.20 | Fall | The pieces turn slowly and fade before they reach the floor; colour comes back from the bell's centre outward; the ash starts falling again | `#e8c46a` to transparent |
| 4.20-5.00 | Fade | The cloud ring closes; a few gold motes settle on the kneeling place | to transparent |

Budget (Story class): 8 pooled meshes (the bell, the shard bell, cloud ring, toll ring, heat wall, shockwave, crack ray card, kneel floor ring) + 60 shards + 40 rays and motes + 30 cloud flakes = 130 particles at most (72 on Normal; the frozen ash is the world's own, not new), 2 effect lights (the bell's steady gold glow from the first toll; the shatter's; × 0.65 on Normal), 2 ribbons (the two toll rings' trailing edges), 1 impact frame at t = 3.00. Peak 2.0 s (the first toll to the shatter) inside the class's 4 s. The kneeling boss makes no attack, so no tell can be hidden; if its rest means it isn't knelt, the bell goes 50% translucent within 2 m of its weapon. Reduced motion: the impact frame becomes a 30% darken, no shake, the ink grade fades in and out over 0.3 s instead of following the ring, and the frozen ash fades out rather than hanging.

## Sound

New `abilityBell`, built on the game's `bellToll` (the great bell, a deep strike with inharmonic partials and a very long ring), close and loud: during the fall a rising air rush (pink noise, high-pass sweeping 200 Hz to 3 kHz over 1 s). The first toll is `bellToll` at gain × 1.4 with a cracked buzz on it (two partials at 220 and 221.5 Hz beating) and a sub swell (sine 36 Hz, 2 s); from it until the shatter the sfx bus is low-passed to 1.8 kHz (World of Ink's muffle), so the bell's hum is the clearest sound in the world. The second toll starts the same and is cut off after 0.15 s by a crack (white noise burst, 30 ms) into a cascade of bronze pieces (many short inharmonic pings at 2-6 kHz over 0.8 s) and a deep drop (sine 40 to 22 Hz, 1.2 s). Then 0.3 s of near silence, and the room's sound and the ash's hiss come back.

## Camera

`CONFIG.camera.feel.powers.bellCall = [-2.0, 0.08]` at the first toll (the view pulls in as the world stops) and `bellToll = [5.0, 0.3]` at the shatter, the biggest kick in the game (still under `maxFov` 6). Lock-on keeps the kneeling boss framed; the camera never leaves the player.

## Images

- `img/bell-of-waking-1.webp`: a colossal ghostly cracked bronze bell of gold light descending from the sky over a kneeling boss on a frozen lake, a white toll ring rolling across the world, everything drained to ink except the gold bell and the swordsman's red scarf.
- `img/bell-of-waking-2.webp`: falling ash frozen in mid-air around the swordsman as a toll ring passes, the world drained of colour, only the red scarf in colour.
- `img/bell-of-waking-3.webp`: the second toll: the giant bell shattering into gold fragments over the boss, a white shockwave across the frozen lake.

docs.about:
# The ability pool

The complete design of Combat Arena 3D's abilities: 110 for Boss Rush and Story's four on top, ready for the iterate
loop to build in the order of `BUILD-ORDER.md`. Design only: nothing here is in the game yet.

- `STYLE.md`: the style bible every effect, card and image is judged against.
- `<id>.md`: one spec per ability (idea, card, data entry, engine work, multiplayer, effect layers and budget, sound,
  camera, images).
- `pool.json`: every ability's core data in one file, written by `node design/abilities/tools/build.cjs` from
  `tools/pool.cjs`, which also checks the card-text cap and the counts below. Change an ability in `tools/pool.cjs`,
  rebuild, then update its spec.
- `CUTS.md`: what left the current 38 and why. `BUILD-ORDER.md`: the batches, one loop pass each.
- `img/`: the concept images (WebP). Full-quality originals sit in `originals/` (gitignored, on Aleix's PC).

## The bars (Aleix, PLAN.md item 6)

- Legendaries are OP, at one level only, with Thunder Call's lightning dragon as the floor: strong enough to turn a
  fight, not to win it alone.
- No rarity cap. Plain stat buffs are at most a third of the commons. Every ability does something no other does.
- Card text is the trigger and the effect only, at most 9 words and 56 characters (`js/validate.js`).
- The feel is anime techniques: "an anime character directing abilities and coordinating to kill the boss".

## Counts

| | Common | Rare | Legendary | All |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Key 1, Strike | | 13 | | 13 |
| Key 2, Guard | | 13 | | 13 |
| Key 3, Summon | | 13 | | 13 |
| Key 4, Ultimate | | | 13 | 13 |
| Triggered (no key) | 26 | 20 | 12 | 58 |
| **All** | **26** | **59** | **25** | **110** |

- Plain stat commons: 8 of 26 (under a third). The other 18 commons each do a small visible thing.
- Summons: 16 (13 on key 3, plus Stone Guardian, Ember Twin and Shade Host). Each is its own Blender model.
- Kept or redesigned from the current 38: 36. New: 74. Cut: 2 (`CUTS.md`).
- Crate-only: Grave Feast and Iron Mercy (as now).
- Story's four, one per key, at the legendary bar: Scarlet Draw (key 1, chapter 2), Oath Guard (key 2, chapter 5),
  The Seven (key 3, chapter 6), Bell of Waking (key 4, chapter 14).

## Rules every spec follows

- Content is data (`js/data/abilities.js`); a new trigger (`when`) or effect (`then`) is an engine addition named in
  the spec's Engine work, with its `validate.js` check.
- Multiplayer: an ability touches only enemies and its holder. A teammate gets at most a small shared benefit (Moon
  Dome's shelter, Still Water's pool, Kindred Ember's revive). Nothing slows, moves, links or takes over a teammate's
  fight. The server resolves powers from range- and rate-checked claims.
- No ability cracks a boss's guard by itself: the counters and the Finishing Blow are the player's. Abilities feed
  them instead.
- Effects use pooled meshes, stay in their budget class on Normal (`STYLE.md`), and keep flashes under 3 Hz with a
  reduced-motion version.

## Rarity colours

Common bone ink `#cfc8b6`, rare cool blue `#8fb8dc`, legendary ember orange `#e59a5c` (`js/config.js`). Story's four:
scarf crimson `#b3262e` and oath gold `#e8c46a`.
docs.style: # Style bible: the look of a technique Every ability's effect, card and image is judged against this page. The images in `img/style-*.webp` show it. ## The references, and what each gives us Feel only. Never a show's or game's names, symbols, characters, crests, costumes or signature looks (VISION.md). | Reference | What we take | What we leave | | --- | --- | --- | | Demon Slayer's elemental breathing forms | Elements as **flat, hard-edged shapes with dark ink outlines and 2-3 tones**: water as a painted wave with foam claws, fire as solid tongues with dark inner lines. The effect follows the blade's path. | Its specific forms, the woodblock wave copied whole, its colours per character. | | Jujutsu Kaisen's techniques | **Impact frames**: one or two frames where the image inverts to two tones, then snaps back. Domain-style moments where the world itself changes colour. Black sparks of a perfect hit. | Its domains' designs, hand signs, any named technique. | | Naruto Shippuden's fights | **Clones, flash steps, held anticipation poses**, the hand sign before the big one, speed lines behind a dash, the wide shot after the hit. | Its symbols, headbands, specific jutsu shapes. | | Sekiro | **Pace**: the deflect spark, the posture moment, the follow-up within half a second. Effects that peak at once and get out of the way. | Its prosthetic tools and kanji prompts. | | Stellar Blade | **Clean, fast VFX on dark ground**: bright cyan and ember cut lines, sharp particles, the camera tightening on a perfect counter. | Its characters and HUD. | ## The rules the images share 1. **The world is dark; the technique is the brightest, most saturated thing on screen.** Arena ash-grey and blue-black, falling ash, dim light. The effect lights the scene. 2. **Hard edges.** Effect shapes are solid, flat-shaded in 2-3 tones with a dark ink outline or a white hot core. No soft fog glow as the main shape (glow is the halo, not the body). 3. **Rarity colour leads the silhouette.** The colour sits on the outer edge of the shape, where the eye reads it first. - Common, bone ink `#cfc8b6`: grey, white and black brush ink. Small: one stroke, one spark. - Rare, cool blue `#8fb8dc`: blue edges, white core, black ink lines. - Legendary, ember orange `#e59a5c`: ember edges over white-hot or white-violet cores, with black ink. - Story, crimson and gold (`#b3262e` scarf red, `#e8c46a` oath gold): the four gifts of the road. 4. **Brush and speed lines.** Ink-brush smears trail the blade; radial speed lines behind dashes and dives; calligraphy strokes for still, precise techniques. 5. **Held poses.** Anticipation (a still beat before the big one), follow-through (a held pose after it, the effect blooming behind). The image is always a keyframe, never a mid-motion blur of nothing. 6. **The delayed cut.** A line hangs in the air, then opens. The signature of our blade techniques. 7. **Few, big, sharp particles.** Streaks, shards, petals, flakes with hard edges. Never a haze of tiny dots. 8. **One impact frame per moment.** Legendaries get one inverted two-tone frame at their peak; nothing else does. Never more than one flash per second from abilities, under 3 Hz in all (VISION). 9. **Boss tells are never hidden.** No effect covers a boss's wind-up for more than 0.3 s; big ones go translucent near the boss's weapon. ## Timing | Phase | Common | Rare | Legendary | Story | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Anticipation | none | 0-0.15 s | 0.2-0.6 s (held pose, the world dims 20%) | 0.4-1.0 s | | Peak | within 0.1 s | within 0.15 s | within 0.2 s of the release | within 0.2 s | | Fade | 0.2-0.6 s | 0.4-1.5 s | 0.5-1.5 s (auras longer) | 1-2 s | ## Budgets on the Normal preset From `js/config.js`: Normal has `fxBudgets.normal` density 0.55, capacity 0.55, ribbons 4, ribbonSub 2, light 0.65, and two pooled effect lights. Every effect uses pooled meshes from the `VIS.abilityFx` pool, made at load and warmed by `visuals.warmUp`; nothing is allocated per cast. | Class | Meshes | Particles (Ultra; Normal × 0.55) | Effect lights | Ribbons | Impact frame | Peak length | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Common | ≤ 3 | ≤ 24 | 0 | 0 | no | ≤ 0.6 s | | Rare | ≤ 8 | ≤ 60 | 1 | ≤ 1 | no | ≤ 1.5 s | | Rare summon | the model + ≤ 4 | ≤ 40 | 1 while striking | ≤ 1 | no | its time | | Legendary | ≤ 20 | ≤ 160 | 2 | ≤ 2 | 1 | ≤ 3 s peak | | Legendary aura (long) | ≤ 4 | ≤ 30 | 1 | 0 | no | its time | | Story | ≤ 28 | ≤ 200 | 2 | 2 | 1 | ≤ 4 s | Reduced motion (`reducedMotion()`): the impact frame becomes a 30% darken, no camera shake, speed lines hold still, the world-colour changes fade in over 0.3 s instead of cutting. ## Camera `CONFIG.camera.feel.powers` maps each power to `[fov kick, dip]` (blast `[4, 0.24]`, lightning `[1.6, 0]`, freeze `[-3.2, 0.05]`). New powers get an entry. Within `powerNear` (26 m) only. Never take the camera from the player: kicks and dips only, at most 0.4 s, and never for commons. ## Sound Synthesised and layered in `js/data/audio.js`, like `abilityBlast` and `abilityDragon`. Each spec names its layers: a transient (the hit), a body (the element), a tail (the room). Pick pitch by rarity (`ABILITY_PICK_PITCH`: common 1, rare 0.84, legendary 0.67). ## Cards The card on the pick screen: the rarity colour on its edge and icon, the 48×48 line icon (`ABILITY_ICONS`), the name, the card text. Hover plays a short loop of how the ability activates (the trigger, then the effect, 1.2-2 s, looping), drawn in the icon's line style on the card's dark face. Commons: one stroke loop. Rares: the trigger and the effect in blue. Legendaries: ember, with a single brighter frame at the effect's peak. Story: crimson and gold. ## The image prompt Every image is made from one preamble plus the subject. The preamble: > Concept art keyframe for an original dark fantasy action game, 16:9 landscape, anime action style: hard-edged cel-shaded effect shapes with dark ink outlines, ink-brush smears, speed lines, a held dramatic pose, low cinematic camera. A dark ash-grey and blue-black stone arena under falling ash, lit mostly by the technique itself, which is the most saturated thing in the frame. The hero is a lone swordsman in a dark hooded coat with a long red scarf and a round shield, face hidden in shadow. Original designs only: no existing characters, logos, symbols, text, letters or watermarks. Then: `Technique colour: . Scene: . Boss: .` Bosses rotate through the game's own: a huge antlered beast of hunger, a chained jailer giant, a bell-ringing warden in robes, a knight of ash, a many-armed witch, a stone colossus. Commons may drop the boss for a close-up of the hero. ## Judging an image Keep it when: the technique reads as one clear shape at a glance; the rarity colour leads; the world stays dark; the hero matches (hood, red scarf, round shield); nothing copies a known show or game; no text. Redo only when it truly misses one of these (a wrong subject, a plain copy, text in the image, the effect unreadable).

# What changes in the current 38

Of the 38 abilities in `js/data/abilities.js`, 36 stay (most redesigned to the new bar) and 2 are cut.

## Cut

| Ability | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Swift Charge (common, charged heavies charge faster) | A plain stat with nothing to see, and the commons may hold only a third plain stats. Hot Iron replaces it on the same action: a full heavy that sprays molten sparks rewards the charge you can see. |
| Long Shadow (common, dashes dodge longer) | A plain stat that blunts the perfect dodge, the skill the counters are built on: longer i-frames make timing matter less, and the bosses' combos are tuned around the dash as it is. Light Step, Hunter's Pace, Ringing Steel and Last Breath already cover the dash, each with something to see. |

## Redesigned

| Ability | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Storm King | No longer draws the lightning dragon, so Thunder Call alone owns it (and the showcase's key-4 beat). A full heavy calls a crown of six bolts that fall in a ring round the boss and converge. |
| Gale Crescent | No longer throws the wind crescent Wind Blade throws. Every eighth hit spins a cage of crescents round the boss for two seconds. |
| Cataclysm | The same blast, now with its own moment: the blade driven into the ground, a ring of ember cracks, a dome of white fire that bursts. |
| Fire Burst | A lotus of flame petals opening under the boss and snapping shut, in place of a plain flare. |
| Counterstep | The perfect dodge flash-steps you behind the boss, in place of making the next hit a riposte (the counter already does that now). |
| Opportunist | Hits on a cracked guard do more, in place of "boss off balance" (the off-balance state left with the stagger bar). |
| Cold Riposte | "Counters" in place of "ripostes" on the card; a frost line on the counter's cut. |
| All legendaries | One level only (Aleix). The data moves from two levels to one; `CONFIG.abilities.rarity.legendary.levels` goes to 1. |
| Every ability | Card texts re-cut to the trigger and the effect; each gets its look, sound, camera and hover loop per its spec. |

## Kept as they are, with their new look

Keen Edge, Iron Blood, Breaker, Static Edge, Light Step, Quick Draught, Keen Eye, Headsman, Vengeance, Bloodthirst, Last Breath, Bastion,
Patience, Counterflame, Stone Guardian, Grave Hound, Lancer of Ash, Wind Blade, Mending, Iron Stance, Grave Feast,
Iron Mercy, Meteor Fall, Time Rift, Thousand Blades, Blood Moon, Pyre, Ember Twin, Thunder Call.

# Build order

One batch per iterate-loop pass, plainest effects first, so each pass lands a working, playable slice and the
engine pieces later batches need arrive before them. Within a batch, abilities that share a new trigger (`when`) or
effect (`then`) are built together. Each spec's Engine work names what it needs.

| Pass | Batch | Abilities | Engine pieces it adds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | The data pass | Legendaries to one level; cut Swift Charge and Long Shadow; new card texts for the kept 36 (Cold Riposte, Counterstep, Opportunist); the plain commons Keen Edge, Iron Blood, Light Step, Quick Draught, Breaker, Keen Eye, Cold Riposte, Headsman with their small touches | `CONFIG.abilities.rarity.legendary.levels = 1`, save-format bump if owned abilities change shape, validate.js for the new texts |
| 2 | Commons I: the blade | Spark Step, Ember Lick, Hot Iron, Petal Cut, Echo Step, Dust Devil | triggers `dashPast`, `stringEnd`, `dashStrike`, `jump`; the common effect pool (≤3 meshes) |
| 3 | Commons II: the guard and the run | Ringing Steel, Thorn Guard, Ash Veil, Bitter Draught, Grit, Kindling, Tithe, Glint, Hunter's Pace, Kindred Ember, Mirror Shard, Shatter Guard | triggers `ready`, `fightStart`, `revive`, `parryShot`, `crack`; key-charge gain hooks |
| 4 | Rares I: the kept perks | Counterstep, Vengeance, Bloodthirst, Last Breath, Opportunist, Bastion, Patience, Counterflame, Static Edge, Grave Feast, Iron Mercy | `flashBehind`, the `cracked` state; each gets its blue look |
| 5 | Rares II: the new triggers | Riptide, Petal Storm, Ironclad, Overcharge, Echoing Blade, Moonfall Cut, Iron Cyclone, Hunting Call | the `wave` line hit (shared with Tidal Arc), `cast`, `comboHeavy`, `summonHit` |
| 6 | Strike I: shapes on the ground | Fire Burst, Wind Blade, Tidal Arc, Frost Spike, Stone Fist, Rising Fang, Thunderclap | line, cone and point area hits; the key-1 effect pool |
| 7 | Strike II: the flashy ones | Sparrow Flurry, Whirl Drill, Shadow Stitch, Spinning Blade, Three Shadows, Quick Draw | multi-hit over time, the returning projectile, clone silhouettes, the delayed cut |
| 8 | Guard I: on yourself | Mending, Iron Stance, Iron Root, Unbroken, Vanishing Step, Ember Mail, Still Water | stance and armour states, the undying floor, the heal pool |
| 9 | Guard II: on the boss | Mirror Ward, Ash Husk, Moon Dome, Waiting Blade, Hourglass, Binding Seal | blow reflection, decoys, shot blocking, the counter stance, path rewind, cancelling a boss's next attack |
| 10 | Summons I | Grave Hound, Lancer of Ash (rebuilt as models), Cinder Fox, Lantern Spirit, Stone Guardian | summon model loading and animation; four Blender models |
| 11 | Summons II | Ink Crows, Bone Archer, Thunder Hawk, Night Owl | flying and ranged summons; marks on the boss |
| 12 | Summons III | Ronin Shade, Mire Serpent, Puppet Knight, Ash Bear, Glass Mantis | the summon's deflect, the coil, strings to the hand |
| 13 | Legendaries I: the kept and redesigned | Meteor Fall, Time Rift, Thousand Blades, Blood Moon, Pyre, Ember Twin, Storm King (bolt crown), Gale Crescent (blade cage) | the impact frame (one per moment, reduced-motion darken) |
| 14 | Legendaries II: new triggered | Hundred Suns, Thunder God Step, Fourfold, Shade Host | `castUltimate`, the lightning dash, the clone host |
| 15 | Ultimates I | Thunder Call (to the new bar), Cataclysm (redesign), Heaven's Lance, Frozen Lotus, Tempest | the long-aura budget, world dim on release |
| 16 | Ultimates II | Great Wave, Sky Blade, Phoenix Dive, Black Star | the player transform (phoenix), the hold-then-implode |
| 17 | Ultimates III | World of Ink, Severance, Colossus, Ash Legion | the world-colour change, the screen-wide cut, the giant and the legion models |
| 18 | Story's four | Scarlet Draw, Oath Guard, The Seven, Bell of Waking | given in chapters 2, 5, 6 and 14; the Seven's and the Bell's models |

Story's four ship with the story passes that build their chapters if those come first; their specs stand alone.
